The State Election Commission told the Court that unforeseen delays in the final publication of the Assembly rolls on 27 October, and the Election Commission's not supplying complete and authenticated roll data since then, had disrupted its schedule. It said it needs the full data, with the additions, deletions, transpositions and corrections, to divide the rolls by ward and to map, verify and publish them. Deccan Herald reports that the data had still not been supplied when the application was filed. It estimated that if it had to wait for the new rolls it would need at least two months after receiving the data to prepare the ward rolls and another month to hold the elections. It said it had already prepared and published rolls for the five corporations from the data of 1 October 2025 that the Election Commission had supplied, and had printed and distributed state voter identity cards on that basis. On 5 November it had told the five corporations to prepare ward rolls from the final rolls of 27 October (protest-66).
commission_reply: Deccan Herald gives no response from the Election Commission or from the state government, and no date on which the Court will hear the application.

what_happened: Justice Krishna Rao of the Calcutta High Court agreed to hear a petition by an Indian Army aspirant who asks for a domicile certificate so that he can take part in the second phase of the Army's recruitment process, LiveLaw reported on 13 November. The petitioner says the authorities refused him the certificate because his mother's name was deleted from the roll in the revision. He told the court that his father's name is still on the roll after the revision, and that he has only just turned 21 and his own name has not yet been registered in the revision. Without the certificate he cannot go further in the recruitment process. The court listed the matter for hearing.
commission_reply: LiveLaw gives no response from the State or from the authority that issues domicile certificates, and no date for the hearing.

what_happened: The Week, carrying a PTI report, said the Jharkhand Assembly passed a resolution opposing the SIR, moved by Parliamentary Affairs Minister Radhakrishna Kishore on behalf of the INDIA bloc. The BJP opposed it. When a Congress member asked for a vote, the Speaker ruled that it stood passed because the ruling coalition had a majority.

The Siasat Daily, carrying a PTI report, said the Kerala Assembly unanimously passed a resolution moved by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan against the SIR in the state, with the Congress-led opposition backing it.

The Punjab Vidhan Sabha passed a resolution by voice vote on 23 October asking for an independent and impartial inquiry into alleged irregularities in voter lists, the electoral process and the functioning of the Election Commission under the Chief Election Commissioner, The Indian Express reported. The paper calls it the first resolution of its kind by an Assembly against the Chief Election Commissioner. Members of the Congress, the Shiromani Akali Dal and the BJP were not in the House when it passed. These are the resolution's and the speakers' allegations.
commission_reply: The report carries no response from the Commission or the BJP.

what_happened: ETV Bharat reported that a Bihar bandh called by the INDIA bloc parties against the SIR disrupted life across much of the state, with Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav taking part.

Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said opposition members protested against the SIR inside the Bihar Assembly on the first day of its monsoon session, with CPI(ML) Liberation legislators wearing black.
ETV Bharat reported that INDIA bloc MPs protested at the Makar Dwar of Parliament against the Bihar SIR for a fifth day running and demanded that it be rolled back.

parties_and_bodies: INDIA bloc; Congress; Police; Election Commission
issues: Protest and march; Police and FIRs
what_happened: The Wire reported that Delhi Police detained opposition MPs, among them Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, when their march from Parliament to the Election Commission against the Bihar SIR was stopped, and that they were released in the afternoon.
commission_reply: The Wire reported that the Commission had written to Jairam Ramesh the day before asking for the names of 30 members for a meeting “due to limitation of space”.

what_happened: ETV Bharat reported that Rahul Gandhi began a 16-day Vote Adhikar Yatra from Sasaram against the SIR in Bihar, due to end with a rally in Patna on 1 September. The Congress leader alleged that the SIR was being done to steal votes.

The News Minute reported that an all-party meeting chaired by Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, attended by nearly 50 parties, resolved to approach the Supreme Court against the SIR in Tamil Nadu. The AIADMK and the BJP were not invited and several other parties stayed away.
ETV Bharat reported that Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee led a procession in Kolkata against the SIR. She called the SIR an assault on people's existence and democratic rights.
Akashvani News reported that the DMK and its alliance partners held protest demonstrations across Tamil Nadu against the SIR, with MPs, MLAs and district functionaries taking part.
The Tribune reported that Mamata Banerjee led a three-km march from Bongaon to Thakurnagar in North 24 Parganas against the SIR, after addressing a rally at Bangaon.
commission_reply: The Tribune reported that the Commission granted a five-member TMC delegation a meeting on 28 November.

parties_and_bodies: Congress; Election Commission; Government of Assam
issues: Protest and march; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: The Siasat Daily, carrying a PTI report, said the united opposition held a protest at Chachal in Guwahati against alleged irregularities in the draft rolls of Assam's Special Revision. Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi accused Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma of misusing the Election Commission.
commission_reply: The report said the Commission stated that the flagged names had not yet been deleted and would only be processed after formal applications in the claims and objections period.

parties_and_bodies: Samajwadi Party; District Election Officer; Election Commission
issues: Protest and march; Pre-printed forms; Form 7
what_happened: The Samajwadi Party demonstrated at the Sultanpur Collectorate on 3 February 2026 and gave the District Magistrate a memorandum for the Chief Election Commissioner, Dainik Bhaskar reported. The party alleged that pre-printed Form 7s in one handwriting were being submitted in bulk against voters from backward, Dalit and minority communities, and asked for them to be cancelled and for FIRs under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

ETV Bharat reported that trade unions, women's groups, student bodies and Dalit and minority rights groups protested against the SIR at Freedom Park in Bengaluru under the banner My Vote, My Right, and urged the state government to take a stand.

issues: Protest and march; Adjudication and appeals
what_happened: ETV Bharat reported that Mamata Banerjee ended her sit-in against the SIR on its fifth day after the Supreme Court ordered appellate tribunals to hear appeals against exclusions in West Bengal. She said the protest was suspended temporarily.

ETV Bharat reported that a Congress delegation led by Kumari Selja staged a sit-in outside the Election Commission headquarters in Delhi over the SIR in Uttarakhand after saying it was not allowed into the premises.

Business Today reported that Congress workers protested in several states demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the handling of the SIR, after The Indian Express reported objections recorded by two Election Commissioners.
commission_reply: Business Today reported that the Commission rejected the characterisation of these exchanges as institutional dissent and said final decisions on the SIR were unanimous.

what_happened: Business Today reported that police detained Assam Congress president and MP Gaurav Gogoi during a protest in Guwahati demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.

parties_and_bodies: Civil society groups; CPI(ML) Liberation; Police
what_happened: The Quint reported that police detained protesters from civil society groups and student organisations at Jantar Mantar, among them CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, as they demanded the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation and a rollback of the SIR.

ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said police detained Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai and hundreds of party workers in Lucknow after they were stopped while marching to demand the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.

ThePrint, carrying an ANI report, said police used water cannons on Congress workers in Patna who were protesting against the Chief Election Commissioner as part of the party's nationwide programme over the SIR.
commission_reply: The report said the Commission described operational queries and internal feedback as part of the normal functioning of a multi-member body and said all final SIR decisions were unanimous.

what_happened: ThePrint, carrying an ANI report, said police used water cannons on Punjab Congress workers demonstrating in Chandigarh as part of the party's protests over the SIR.

ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said the Himachal Pradesh Congress protested outside the Election Commission office in Shimla, burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner and raised slogans against the SIR.

UNI reported that Congress workers in Shillong, led by state Congress president Vincent H. Pala, burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner and demanded his removal amid the row over the SIR.

issues: Protest and march; Names left off or deleted; Form 7
what_happened: Asianet Newsable reported that the Uttarakhand Congress marched in Dehradun, surrounded the Election Commission office and burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner. The party raised concerns over how names were added and deleted and how objections were disposed of.

ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said the Karnataka Congress, with Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, protested at Freedom Park in Bengaluru against the SIR and demanded the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.
commission_reply: The Election Commission, however, has asserted that its official orders, decisions and administrative directions have full legal sanction, and that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberations within any institution.

what_happened: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said police used water cannons and detained former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot and state Congress chief Govind Singh Dotasra during a march to the State Election Commission office in Jaipur over alleged SIR irregularities.

Leaders of the INDIA bloc, 33 of them from 19 parties, agreed a plan of district marches from 2 to 8 October, a march of opposition MPs to the Commission on 6 October, a meeting with the President in the second week of October and five rallies including one in Delhi on 1 November, The Wire reported. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the Commission was being used as a puppet by the Prime Minister and the Home Minister.

The South First reported that more than a dozen civil society groups held a day-long protest at Dharna Chowk in Hyderabad, demanding that the SIR be scrapped and the Chief Election Commissioner resign.

The Free Press Journal reported that Uddhav Thackeray of the Shiv Sena (UBT) and Raj Thackeray of the MNS led the Virat Garjana Morcha in Mumbai seeking the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation. Raj Thackeray demanded that the SIR in Maharashtra be cancelled.

issues: Protest and march; Police and FIRs
what_happened: The Wire reported that police stopped an INDIA bloc march from Parliament to the Election Commission, and that opposition MPs held a sit-in at the All India Radio building until police detained Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra that night.

Opposition MPs of the INDIA bloc marched from Parliament to the Commission's headquarters to press for the Chief Election Commissioner's removal, and asked for 240 MPs to meet the three Commissioners at Parliament House Annexe, Deccan Herald reported.
commission_reply: The Commission said no party had sought an appointment until 4 pm, that a meeting of 240 MPs away from its premises was unusual and could not be accepted, and that the MPs declined its offer to send its senior-most officer on duty to receive their memorandum, Deccan Herald reported.

what_happened: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said AAP workers and members of other parties protested outside the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over alleged SIR irregularities. It said AAP had earlier protested at Jantar Mantar and India Gate.

parties_and_bodies: INDIA bloc; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi; Congress; Police
issues: Protest and march; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: The Tribune reported that Delhi leaders of the INDIA bloc marched to the Election Commission office and gave the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer a memorandum demanding that the SIR be cancelled and excluded eligible voters be restored. It said police detained Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav at a separate protest at Jantar Mantar.

An INDIA bloc delegation including Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi gave President Droupadi Murmu a memorandum after opposition MPs marched from Parliament House and were stopped by police at Vijay Chowk, PTI reported. Kharge said the President had asked for evidence, which the bloc would provide, and Rahul Gandhi said she had not denied what they told her and that the leaders would meet the Chief Justice on Monday. The News Mill reported that the memorandum asked for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation, repeal of the 2023 law on the Commissioners, suspension of the SIR with the names the bloc says were left off or deleted illegally put back, a return to paper ballots, and annulment of Assembly elections of the past two years where it said evidence of vote theft had been presented. These are the INDIA bloc's demands and allegations.
commission_reply: No response from Rashtrapati Bhavan or the Commission to the memorandum was reported.

what_happened: The South First reported on the morning of 10 October that police sealed central Delhi before the Cockroach Janta Party's protest at Jantar Mantar demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over the SIR. It said more than 1,000 people had been detained overnight and 45 Metro stations were shut, and that police detained CPI(M) leaders including Pinarayi Vijayan and John Brittas when they tried to march from Kerala House.
commission_reply: No statement from the Commission was reported. Police told the protesters that a gathering of more than four people was not allowed.

what_happened: The Delhi Police told the Delhi High Court on 13 October that it de-notified Jantar Mantar as the designated protest site, and identified three other sites, on the basis of the Supreme Court's order of 9 October, Bar and Bench reported. That order had said suitable sites where basic amenities could be provided to protesters should be identified, and left the decision to the competent authority. The submission came on Indian Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib's petition against the refusal of permission to protest at Jantar Mantar against the Chief Election Commissioner. Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice on three of its prayers, which challenge the police's reliance on its 2022 standing order and the 10-day advance notice for protests.
commission_reply: The police said the petition had become infructuous because Jantar Mantar had been de-notified. On 15 October the Solicitor General told the Supreme Court that the decision followed the recommendations of a committee set up by the Union Home Ministry well before the Court's oral observations, Bar and Bench reported.

what_happened: Counsel for two traders' associations raised in the Supreme Court on 16 October their petition against the Cockroach Janta Party's call to unfurl the tricolour in Connaught Place's Central Park that evening, saying it would obstruct trade worth Rs 200 crore a day, The Wire reported. The party had called the protest after two of its leaders were arrested for waving the flag at Jantar Mantar. The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said it would act on compensation if the NDMC's restrictions were found disproportionate, noted that the Delhi High Court was hearing a similar matter, and listed the petition for 26 and 27 October, after the Dussehra break.
commission_reply: The Wire says the petitions appear to be concerned with the protest itself, though counsel told the Court the NDMC had shut the place by a notice the night before, as LiveLaw reported. It carries the party founder's post on X that businesses suffer when the government shuts down a city and restricts its citizens' movement.

issues: Protest and march; Police and FIRs
what_happened: Chennai police arrested students and youth activists who began a 24-hour sit-in against the revision near Rajarathinam Stadium in Egmore at 4 pm on 22 October in defiance of a police ban, The Hindu reported. Nine organisations, among them Left student and youth groups and the Cockroach Janta Party, had formed a platform called Chennai's Jantar Mantar 2.0 and asked for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation. They were held overnight at a community hall and released the next morning at the stadium, where they resumed the protest.
commission_reply: The report carries no statement from the police beyond the ban.

issues: Protest and march; Police and FIRs; Commission's independence
what_happened: Delhi Police detained more than 150 people on 23 October at a march in central Delhi against the revision and the Chief Election Commissioner, called by the Delhi Coordination Committee of People Against SIR, The Indian Express reported. About 300 people gathered near Gole Dak Khana around 2 pm and marched towards Gurdwara Bangla Sahib. When they could not reach the Commission's office they held a sit-in near the roundabout, and security forces began detaining them by 3 pm. The paper also reported that over 57 cases registered during the protests of 2 to 15 October had been moved to the Crime Branch.
commission_reply: A senior police officer said the cases were moved because they needed close technical investigation and thorough questioning.

issues: Names left off or deleted; Protest and march
what_happened: Representatives of the Left Democratic Front walked out of an all-party meeting called by Kerala's Chief Electoral Officer on 23 October for the Special Summary Revision, The Hindu reported, and asked that the names of 24.08 lakh voters left off the draft roll of the state's earlier revision be put back. The paper reports that 24.08 lakh is the fall at the draft stage and that the final roll of 21 February 2026 was 8.97 lakh below the roll of October 2025.
commission_reply: The Chief Electoral Officer, D. Sajith Babu, said he had told the leaders he would convey to the Commission their demand that the 2 November deadline for rationalising polling stations be extended.

parties_and_bodies: Congress; Trinamool Congress; CPI(M); CPI(ML) Liberation
issues: Adjudication and appeals; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: The Congress, the Trinamool Congress, the CPI(M), the CPI(ML) Liberation, civil rights organisations and public figures gave West Bengal's State Election Commissioner a memorandum on 26 October asking that elections to the Kolkata and Howrah municipal corporations be held only after electors deleted in the revision have been heard, The Wire reported. They asked the State Election Commission to use its powers under Section 5 of the West Bengal State Election Commission Act, 1994 to add to the civic rolls everyone whose appeal is pending before the SIR appellate tribunals. Citing the Election Commission's affidavit of 16 September in the Supreme Court, the memorandum puts the pending appeals at about 1.2 lakh in the Kolkata Municipal Corporation area and about 39,000 in the Howrah Municipal Corporation area. It asks that the polls wait until the re-enrolment drive and the Special Summary Revision, whose final roll is due on 4 January 2027, are complete.
commission_reply: The State Election Commissioner's office said he would meet a delegation of the signatories on 28 October, according to their press release as The Wire reports it. No reply from the State Election Commission on the substance was reported.

parties_and_bodies: SIR-Virodhi Karnataka; Government of Karnataka; INDIA bloc
issues: Protest and march; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: SIR-Virodhi Karnataka, a coalition opposed to the revision, asked the State government on 28 October to reject the final roll prepared through the revision and to hold a social audit, public hearings and public scrutiny of the exercise, The Hindu reported. A leader of the coalition told the press, a day after Karnataka's final roll was published, that the State should use the previous roll for the coming local body elections, and called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The coalition said official projections put Karnataka's population aged 18 and above at 5.19 crore in 2026, against about 4.5 crore electors on the final roll, and questioned the fall in Bengaluru's electors, reports of alleged attempts by BJP members to file Form 7 applications in bulk, and the pressure on booth level officers. It said it would protest during the Assembly session that begins on 26 November, after the INDIA bloc's protest against the revision on 1 November.
commission_reply: The report gives no reply from the State government, the Chief Electoral Officer or the Election Commission.

issues: Protest and march; Police and FIRs
what_happened: A division bench of the Bombay High Court, Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna, on 2 November kept in abeyance until 7 December the Leave India Notice that the Foreigners Regional Registration Office issued on 14 October to an actor who is a United States citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India card, The Hindu and The Indian Express reported. Police had detained him near August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai on 10 October at a protest demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner over the SIR. The actor filed an unconditional apology and an undertaking that he would not take part in any protest or influence others to take part. The bench said Overseas Citizen of India cardholders could not claim the same rights as citizens, and The Indian Express reports that it said he was not remotely affected by the SIR. It allowed him to stay in India until the registration office decides the notice after hearing his response, and listed the matter for 7 December.
commission_reply: Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh, for the Union, argued that the actor had been involved in the protest from the start and had no legally enforceable right to remain in India. Senior advocate Venkatesh Dhond, for the actor, said he had gone to the site out of curiosity, had no link with the organisers and had not been heard before the notice was issued.

parties_and_bodies: Disha Students' Organisation; Revolutionary Workers' Party of India; Police; INDIA bloc
issues: Protest and march; Police and FIRs
what_happened: Delhi Police registered an FIR against 22 protesters detained at Minto Road on 1 November as they marched from the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan towards Jantar Mantar, Hindustan Times reported on 3 November. Police said members of the Disha Students' Organisation and the Revolutionary Workers' Party of India took out the march at about 5 pm, that Jantar Mantar is no longer a protest site, and that the protesters were taken in two buses to the Dwarka Sector 23 and Jafarpur Kalan police stations and released by 2 am the next day. The FIR is under Sections 223(a), 132, 221, 121(1), 3(5) and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. An artist affiliated with the party was placed in preventive detention at the Connaught Place police station under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita. Before the Special Executive Magistrate at Mandir Marg he refused to sign a peace bond, and he was released after furnishing sureties and a personal bond. A member of the party said the march demanded that Jantar Mantar be reclaimed as a protest site and that the SIR be scrapped. Hindustan Times had reported on 2 November that police said over 50 protesters were briefly detained near Minto Road after the rally, and the later report does not say whether the 22 are among them.
commission_reply: Members of the two organisations alleged that police dragged protesters, women among them, into the buses and that one woman fainted, and the party said the artist was held for 23 hours and denied medication. The report carries no reply from the police to these allegations.

what_happened: The Kochi Corporation Council passed a resolution on 3 November moved by the United Democratic Front councillor Deepthy Mary Varghese, a general secretary of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee, expressing solidarity with the nationwide protests by political, youth and student groups against alleged irregularities in the SIR, The Hindu reported. The resolution, backed by the Left Democratic Front's leader in the council, V.A. Sreejith, criticised the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, for bringing disrepute to a constitutional office by, as it alleged, stripping more than 13 crore voters of their votes. All six BJP councillors walked out during the discussion. A BJP councillor had said that more than 2.50 crore of the names taken off the rolls were those of dead people, and UDF councillors rose to protest. The Mayor, V.K. Minimol, declared the resolution passed in the absence of the BJP councillors.
commission_reply: The BJP's leader in the council, Sudha Dilipkumar, said UDF councillors had ridiculed BJP councillors and denied them the right to respond, and later accused the Mayor of behaving like a Mahila Congress leader. The Mayor said that holding a discussion before approving the resolution was in keeping with the democratic spirit.

parties_and_bodies: Trinamool Congress; CPI(M); Congress; BJP; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal
what_happened: Leaders of the Trinamool Congress, the Left Front and the Congress asked at an all-party meeting with West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer, Neelam Meena, on 3 November that the 27 lakh electors whose names judicial officers deleted in the revision be allowed to apply again on Form 6, The Times of India reported. They alleged that the Commission was acting at the BJP's behest to have lakhs of names deleted through Form 7, and questioned the 16 lakh appeals filed before the tribunals, which they alleged officials of the Chief Electoral Officer's office had filed to seek the deletion of electors whom judicial officers had cleared. The Trinamool Congress's Kunal Ghosh alleged that the Commission was imposing the special summary revision while appeals from the revision were pending. He said the special roll observer, Subrata Gupta, had said he had no information about the 16 lakh appeals, and that the Chief Electoral Officer had told the parties the appeals were filed before she took charge. The CPI(M)'s Palash Das asked whether Form 7 was a project for the mass deletion of electors in the BJP's interest. The Congress's Ashutosh Chatterjee said the tribunals had been unable to upload their orders since 21 September and that the tribunal for Kolkata had no judge.
commission_reply: The BJP's Sisir Bajoria told the meeting that one elector in the Barabani constituency was linked as father to 389 electors and one in Bally to 310, the paper reported. The report gives no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer to the demand.

parties_and_bodies: Police; CPI; VCK; Civil society groups
what_happened: Members of the Jananayaka Meetpu Kuzhu staged a rail roko near the old railway station in Kanchipuram on 4 November, demanding the arrest of the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, Hindustan Times reported from ANI. The protesters alleged that he had acted in favour of the Prime Minister by "disqualifying 13 crore voters". More than 350 protesters marched from near Hotel Tamil Nadu towards the East Railway Station, where a scuffle broke out when police tried to stop them, and more than 50 sat on the tracks. Police detained all the protesters and held them in a private marriage hall. Members of Makkal Mandram, the Communist Party of India and the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi and independent activists took part, and the report says the protest caused tension in the area for about an hour.
commission_reply: The report carries no statement from the police or the railways and does not say whether a case was registered or when the protesters were released.

issues: Protest and march; Police and FIRs
what_happened: Mumbai Police asked the Foreigners Regional Registration Office to verify the Overseas Citizen of India status of a second actor detained at the protest of 10 October in Mumbai against the Chief Election Commissioner, The Indian Express reported on 4 November. She is a cousin of the actor whose Leave India Notice the Bombay High Court kept in abeyance on 2 November (protest-51). The paper reports that an FIR was registered against her for taking part in the protest, and a police officer told it that she was born in Mumbai and holds an OCI card. A police officer told the paper that the police had written to the registration office after the two were detained, asking that both actors' OCI status be checked, and that on 16 October, two days after the notice to her cousin, they wrote again to say she held an OCI card and that an FIR had been registered against her. The paper reports that the registration office then examined the status of both. The protest was organised by Tushar Gandhi's Hum Bharat Ke Log.
commission_reply: Her cousin's lawyer told The Indian Express that she had not been served a notice by the registration office. The report gives no statement from the registration office.

parties_and_bodies: INDIA bloc; Congress; CPI(M); CPI; CPI(ML) Liberation; Samajwadi Party; Police
issues: Protest and march; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: The INDIA bloc's Karnataka unit held a protest against the SIR at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on 5 November, demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, ANI reported. The Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee president, B.K. Hariprasad, said the protest continued the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on 1 November and would go on until the Chief Election Commissioner resigned. He said District Congress Committee presidents were holding rallies at every district headquarters the same day and that the protest would reach the taluks and blocks from the next day. The Chief Minister, D.K. Shivakumar, said every elector whose name had been deleted, other than those who had died, should get justice. The Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge alleged that the Commission had made five U-turns over its stand on Form 6 and Form 7 and over the software, which he said had been manipulated for deletions. The report names the Congress, the CPI(M), the CPI, the CPI(ML) Liberation, the Forward Bloc and the Samajwadi Party among the organisers, with student, youth and other groups, and gives the protest as running from 11 am to 2 pm.
commission_reply: The report carries no statement from the Election Commission. It says police were deployed at Freedom Park and reports no arrests.

parties_and_bodies: INDIA bloc; Congress; Government of Karnataka; BJP; Police
issues: Protest and march; Form 7; Police and FIRs
what_happened: The INDIA bloc adopted a five-point resolution at its protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on 5 November (protest-55), The Hindu reported. The resolution demands that the SIR be scrapped, that the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, resign and that the revised rolls in Karnataka be rejected. It asks the state government to hold the coming local body, taluk panchayat and zilla panchayat elections on the rolls of 2025, from before the revision, and calls for the repeal of the law on the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner. It puts the fall in Karnataka's roll at 99.32 lakh names, from 5.54 crore to about 4.5 crore in the final roll of 27 October, It says about 23 lakh of these were dead or duplicate electors and alleges that nearly 76 lakh were eligible electors, including migrants and people who had moved house. It alleges that BJP workers misused Form 7 to seek the deletion of names. The Chief Minister, D.K. Shivakumar, announced at the protest that the state government would start a police investigation into the alleged misuse of Form 7, and he alleged that Form 7 applications had been printed at the BJP office and handed to constituency leaders with electors' names and identity details. The state Cabinet discussed the SIR the same day. The Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister, Eshwar Khandre, said afterwards that no decision had been taken on whether the rolls after the revision would be used for the zilla and taluk panchayat elections, and that the State Election Commission would decide and would seek the government's opinion, The Hindu reported.
commission_reply: The reports carry no statement from the Election Commission. The BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra, at a press conference in Bengaluru that The Hindu reported the same evening, denied the Congress's claims and its figures on eligible electors who had lost their votes. Neither report gives an answer from the BJP to the allegation about Form 7.

issues: Names left off or deleted; Living electors marked dead
what_happened: Karnataka's Chief Minister, D.K. Shivakumar, favours a committee to study the final rolls prepared through the revision, Deccan Herald reported, and the Public Works Minister, Satish Jarkiholi, said the Chief Minister was forming one to see whether eligible electors were left out. Some ministers told the Cabinet on 5 November that the revision had not had much effect on deletions in their constituencies. Jarkiholi said the government must decide whether the coming local body elections use the roll prepared through the revision or the one from before it. The Deputy Chief Minister, G. Parameshwara, said the government's stand must agree with the Congress's. He said that in some ministers' constituencies only about 2,000 electors had been left out, and that across the state 1.08 crore electors were left off, 16 lakh of them marked dead, some of whom were apparently alive, and 65 lakh shown as shifted.
commission_reply: The report does not give the committee's members, its terms or a date for it, and carries no statement from the Election Commission or the State Election Commission.

what_happened: Karnataka's State Election Commission directed the commissioners of the five city corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority to speed up the preparation of ward-wise electoral rolls for the elections to the five corporations, Deccan Herald reported on 12 November. In a communication dated 5 November, the State Election Commission told officials to base the rolls on the final Assembly rolls published on 27 October after the revision. Officials are to map electors' details to the notified ward boundaries and prepare the rolls in Excel format, with no more than 1,200 electors in a polling part, and are to send the ward rolls and related details to the State Election Commission by 12 November. The State Election Commission said the work was begun in accordance with the Supreme Court's directions, which set the end of December as the deadline for completing the elections.
commission_reply: The direction is the State Election Commission's own. The report does not name the Supreme Court case or date its order, and it carries no statement from the state government or from the parties that asked for the local body elections to be held on the rolls from before the revision.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi; AAP; CPI; CPI(M); Civil society groups; Election Commission
issues: Names left off or deleted; Form 7; Form 6
what_happened: A delegation of opposition parties and civil society groups met Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer at his office at Kashmiri Gate on 9 November to discuss carrying out the Commission's letter of 6 November on electors left off the draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, The Wire and Hindustan Times reported. The Wire names Amit Mishra of the Aam Aadmi Party, Dinesh Varshney of the CPI, Anurag Saxena of the CPI(M), Shamsher Singh of the CPI(ML), R.S. Dagar of the Revolutionary Socialist Party, Hari Shankar of the All India Forward Bloc, Anjali Bhardwaj of Voter Adhikar Manch and Amrita Johri of Satark Nagrik Sangathan, with members of Voter Adhikar Manch, Jan Sarokar and the Centre for Financial Accountability. By the delegation's statement after the meeting, the Chief Electoral Officer accepted several of its suggestions and issued directions, and a standard operating procedure is to be released shortly. The delegation says he accepted that electors left off the draft and placed on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors published on 31 August can be restored by an enumeration form and keep their earlier serial and EPIC numbers, and that he assured it he would consider giving their earlier EPIC numbers to electors who applied again on Form 6 after 31 August. On Form 7 it asked for verification with the booth level agent who filed each form, publication of every application, notices to affected electors and no decision without a fair hearing. It raised Form 7s it says were wrongly filed in Mustafabad, and it says it was agreed that Form 7s filed by registration officers or assistant registration officers would be examined again. It also asked for enrolment camps in unauthorised colonies, JJ clusters and slum settlements from 7 am and from 7 pm to 10 pm, for the publication of the names deleted before the revision with the reasons, for a fixed time to decide Form 6 applications, for surprise inspections of the booth level officers' work, and for more time for the 47,56,722 electors left off the draft roll to be included. The delegation says it was asked to submit the names of electors its own surveys found wrongly deleted.
commission_reply: Everything the claim says the Chief Electoral Officer accepted, assured or agreed rests on the delegation's own account, and neither report carries a statement from him. A senior official of his office told Hindustan Times that the meeting went well and that the office would work on the suggestion, and said "Several suggestions were already in the pipeline. We will consider all demands which help make the process easier for ordinary voters." Neither report says when the standard operating procedure will be released, and no reply from the Commission was reported.

parties_and_bodies: Karnataka Rajya Muslim Okkoota; Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka
issues: Names left off or deleted; Minorities
what_happened: The Karnataka Rajya Muslim Okkoota, an umbrella body of Muslim community groups, said in a statement on 9 November that an analysis of the Commission's booth level data by the political research consultancy Sankalp found that 27.59% of the electors in the 10 Assembly constituencies represented by Muslim MLAs were left off the roll, against a state average of 19.45%, The Hindu and The Indian Express reported. The statement calls these names deleted. By the body's estimate, those 10 constituencies held 9,62,359 Muslim electors on the 2025 roll, of whom 2,46,759 (25.64%) were left off, and more than 8.80 lakh Muslim electors were left off in 64 constituencies where Muslims are a large share of the population. By the same estimate, 2,58,770 of the 15,15,088 electors left off as absent across the state, and 1,43,940 of the 7,08,666 left off as already enrolled elsewhere, were Muslims. The Indian Express gives the body's shares as 17.1% and 20.3%, against a Muslim share of 12.9% of the state's population and 12.2% of the electors left off as dead. The body argues that a finding of absent or enrolled elsewhere rests on the judgement of booth level officers and other field officials, where a death can be checked against official records. It gives Chamarajpet 1,07,722 names left off, Kalaburagi North 1,05,257, Narasimharaja 99,367 and Shivajinagar 81,230. It asked the Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission to explain, and demanded that the revision be scrapped, that the previous rolls be used for future elections, that a judicial inquiry be held and that legal action be taken against officials found responsible for irregularities.
commission_reply: Neither report carries a reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission.

parties_and_bodies: Booth level officers; Teachers' unions; Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala
issues: BLO workload; Deaths; Protest and march
what_happened: The News Minute reported that hundreds of booth level officers across Kerala stayed away from SIR work on a strike call after the death of a BLO in Kannur, and that employee and teacher action councils marched to collectorates.
commission_reply: The News Minute reported that Kerala's Chief Electoral Officer said he had not received any complaints regarding work pressure from BLOs.

parties_and_bodies: Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu
issues: BLO workload; Schedule and deadlines; Protest and march
what_happened: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said the Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu began a statewide boycott of SIR work over workload, staff shortages, deadline pressure and poor training.

parties_and_bodies: BLO Adhikar Raksha Committee; Police; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal
what_happened: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said booth level officers marching under the BLO Adhikar Raksha Committee clashed with police outside the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office in Kolkata over SIR workload.
commission_reply: Deccan Herald reported that Chief Electoral Officer Manoj Agarwal described the BLOs as the "real heroes" of the exercise.

parties_and_bodies: Uttar Pradeshiya Prathmik Shikshak Sangh; District Election Officer; Booth level officers
issues: BLO workload; Police and FIRs; Software (ECINET/ERONET)
what_happened: The Gautam Buddh Nagar unit of the Uttar Pradesh Primary Teachers' Association wrote to the District Magistrate on 24 November 2025 alleging mental harassment of the about 1,800 teachers deployed as booth officers, two days after FIRs were registered against more than 60 booth officers and seven supervisors under section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, The Indian Express reported. The association asked for the FIRs to be withdrawn and said the Commission's app did not work in rural areas.
commission_reply: The Indian Express reported that the FIRs were lodged on the orders of the District Magistrate and District Election Officer, Medha Rupam, against booth officers alleged to have shown a lack of compliance.

issues: BLO workload; Deaths; Protest and march
what_happened: After a lekhpal supervising the revision died by suicide in Bindki, Fatehpur, the Lekhpal Association protested, would not let the body be taken for post-mortem until a case was registered, and announced a boycott of SIR work unless action was taken, The New Indian Express reported.

The Wire reported that nearly 250 primary school teachers working as booth level officers stopped work and held a sit-in at a data uploading centre in Ahmedabad, alleging threats and pressure during the SIR.

parties_and_bodies: Booth level officers; District Election Officer; Electoral Registration Officer; Uttar Pradeshiya Prathmik Shikshak Sangh; Election Commission
issues: Software (ECINET/ERONET); BLO workload; Police and FIRs
what_happened: Newslaundry reported that Ghaziabad registered an FIR against 21 employees for negligence in booth officer duties on 27 November 2025, after Gautam Buddh Nagar's FIRs, and that glitches in the Commission's mobile application were a main reason for slow digitisation. The Ghaziabad complainant, a deputy tehsildar, admitted the app sometimes hung. The teachers' association letter cited app glitches and repeated OTP failures.
commission_reply: Officials told Newslaundry the FIRs were for negligence. An electoral registration officer said "Those who do not work will face action." Newslaundry said it sent questions to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's office.

parties_and_bodies: Uttar Pradeshiya Prathmik Shikshak Sangh; Teachers' unions
what_happened: Amar Ujala reported that teachers' organisations in Uttar Pradesh, among them the Uttar Pradeshiya Prathmik Shikshak Sangh, objected to the deaths of teachers and staff on SIR duty and demanded jobs and compensation for their families.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; Booth level officers
what_happened: The Punjab and Haryana High Court quashed the suspension of a teacher in Hisar district who had asked to be relieved of booth level officer duty after his wife died, and imposed costs of Rs 50,000 on the District Elementary Education Officer, Hisar and the Electoral Registration Officer for the Barwala constituency, Bar and Bench reported. Justice Harpreet Singh Brar found that the authorities appointed three substitutes for his booth without making sure any of them joined, and then suspended him for a duty he no longer held. The Court directed the Chief Electoral Officer, Haryana to make sure that a booth level officer who is replaced is told in writing whether he stands relieved.
commission_reply: The authorities said he had never been relieved of the duty and had missed the SIR training. The Court found they could not state the date of the training, and noted that none of the three substitutes attended it either.

what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported the Commission saying that about 87 per cent of Bihar's 7.96 crore voters had been given semi-filled enumeration forms on the first booth officer visit.

LiveLaw reported that the Association for Democratic Reforms told the Supreme Court that enumeration forms in Bihar were being uploaded by officials without voters' knowledge or consent. This is ADR's allegation in a court filing.
commission_reply: LiveLaw reported that ADR filed the rejoinder in reply to the Commission's counter-affidavit.

issues: Form 7; Pre-printed forms; Police and FIRs
what_happened: National Herald reported that Trinamool workers stopped a vehicle in Khatra, Bankura said to carry thousands of pre-filled Form 7s, that police seized it and began an inquiry, and that both parties traded allegations over bulk Form 7s on the last day for filing.
commission_reply: National Herald reported that the BJP alleged its workers were attacked and prevented from filing forms inside government offices.

what_happened: Scroll reported that Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra alleged that computer-printed Form 7s were distributed in every constituency and that booth agents' signatures were forged, and demanded a forensic inquiry. These are the Congress's allegations.
commission_reply: Scroll reported that BJP minister Gautam Dak said a voter proposed for deletion gets time to be heard and that the Congress wanted to create a dispute.

issues: Form 7; Pre-printed forms; Notices and hearings
what_happened: Scroll reported that during Assam's Special Revision a booth officer in Karimganj North was handed objections against 133 voters on forms she described as half printed and half handwritten, all in the name of one elector who told Scroll he had not filed them, and that hearings were suspended in three Nagaon constituencies after complaints of fake Form 7s.
commission_reply: Scroll quoted a senior Commission official in Guwahati saying a voter can file any number of objections but that an ERO reviews them individually when one person files more than five.

what_happened: Scroll reported that at least seven people named as objectors on Form 7s in Assam, some of them BJP booth agents and members, said they had not filed the objections.
commission_reply: Scroll quoted BJP MP Kamakhya Prasad Tasa as saying anyone can file objections and that it is for the Election Commission to take a final call.

what_happened: The Indian Express reported that Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma told reporters he had told BJP members to keep filing complaints against people he called 'Miyas' and to fill Form 7s wherever possible during the Special Revision.

ETV Bharat reported that Bhopal's Collector ordered a probe after a man named as objector on Form 7s in Bhopal South-West denied filing them, and that officials found incorrect or fake objector details in several of the district's 9,037 Form 7s.
commission_reply: ETV Bharat quoted District Election Officer Kaushlendra Vikram Singh saying no one's name would be deleted without verification.

what_happened: The Samajwadi Party president alleged on X that pre-printed Form 7s were being distributed in villages to strike off opposition voters, that the objectors listed on them could not be traced and that signatures were forged, The Economic Times reported from ANI. He said voters from backward, Dalit and minority communities were most affected.

Frontline reported that Congress general secretary K. C. Venugopal wrote to the Commission on 29 January alleging misuse of Form 7 in several states, and that the Commission said there was no limit on forms per voter but that an ERO must verify when one person files more than five.
commission_reply: Scroll reported on 23 January 2026 that a senior Commission official in Guwahati gave the same rule.

what_happened: Form 7 objections were filed against 14 voters of one community in part 14 of the Sadar constituency in Sonbhadra, Dainik Bhaskar reported. The booth officer inspected on the spot and found the objections false. Two of the 14 had died and the rest were present. The booth officer told the Samajwadi Party's district secretary that one person had complained and filled in the forms, and the secretary said he would take the case to the District Magistrate.

parties_and_bodies: Booth level officers; Police; Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh
what_happened: Residents of a village in Siddharthnagar went to the Mishrauliya police station to complain that about 86 villagers were being objected to by Form 7, BBC News Hindi reported. The booth officer told local media that one person had handed him all 86 forms, that every voter named in them was Muslim and that all of them were present.
commission_reply: The Chief Electoral Officer told BBC News Hindi "जिन लोगों के नाम कटवाने के लिए फ़ॉर्म 7 मिला है, उन्हें नोटिस दिए बिना और सुनवाई के बगैर नाम नहीं काटे जाएंगे."

parties_and_bodies: Samajwadi Party; Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh; BJP
what_happened: A Samajwadi Party former minister from Gonda said more than 6,000 deletions were being sought in the Karnalganj constituency and showed BBC News Hindi printed Form 7s, one of which carried the district, polling station and constituency already filled in but no objector's name. BBC News Hindi reported that every form had 'already enrolled' ticked as the reason.
commission_reply: At a press conference on 6 February the Chief Electoral Officer said "कोई भी राजनीतिक दल का कार्यकर्ता एक दिन में 10 फ़ॉर्म से ज़्यादा नहीं जमा कर सकता है. जो फ़ॉर्म 7 जमा किए गए हैं, उनकी जांच होगी. अभी कोई नाम नहीं काटे जा रहे हैं." The BJP called the Samajwadi Party's allegations baseless.

parties_and_bodies: Samajwadi Party; BJP; District Election Officer; Election Commission
what_happened: The Samajwadi Party MP for Badaun gave the District Magistrate a list alleging that objections were being filed to a plan, BBC News Hindi reported, including a Form 7 against an elected ward member of Kakrala who said he had been a voter since 2012. In Datganj, a BJP Assembly convener whose name was on an objection told BBC News Hindi he had signed forms the party gave him and did not personally know the voter.
commission_reply: The BJP called the allegations baseless, BBC News Hindi reported, and the Commission said complaints would be examined.

parties_and_bodies: Congress; Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh
what_happened: The Congress said its workers in Sant Kabir Nagar caught Form 7s being submitted to delete villagers and that the man whose signature was on them denied signing, BBC News Hindi reported. BBC News Hindi said it could not verify the video of the incident.
commission_reply: The Chief Electoral Officer said "इस पर उस व्यक्ति को एफ़आईआर दर्ज करानी चाहिए जिनका हस्ताक्षर फर्ज़ी है." He said officers had been told to make sure each Form 7 was submitted by the person whose signature it carried.

issues: Form 7; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: Scroll reported, citing PTI, that after Assam's final roll the Chief Minister said several deletions had been made on complaints filed by BJP workers.

Newslaundry reported that the 15,663 Form 7s in Somnath were filed by 269 people, each filing 50 or more, that copies it reviewed had the voter's details printed in English and the objector's details handwritten in Gujarati, and that six of the objectors filed affidavits saying they had not filed them.
commission_reply: Newslaundry reported that the District Election Officer, V. N. Upadhyay, said he had deployed six AEROs to verify the objections and assured that no name would be deleted arbitrarily.

what_happened: The Quint reported that thousands of Form 7s in Alwar were filed in the names of BJP booth agents, several of whom said their signatures were forged, and that no FIR or inquiry had been announced a month later.
commission_reply: The Quint reported that calls to the District Magistrate and Sub-Divisional Magistrate for comment went unanswered.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal; Electoral Registration Officer
what_happened: National Herald reported that the Commission wrote to West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer to send all Form 7 objections to EROs by 16 February and dispose of them by statutory procedure, and that it had taken cognisance of reports of Form 7 records being burnt.

parties_and_bodies: District Election Officer; Booth level officers
what_happened: Siasat reported, citing The Indian Express, that Form 7s against 544 voters of a Shamli village were found with a booth officer, said to have been already printed with the voters' EPIC numbers. All of them named one applicant, whom officials could not find, and the District Magistrate said the forms were fake and the probe found nothing.
commission_reply: DM Arvind Kumar Chauhan ordered a probe and later said that the case “didn’t have any substance.” “We got an investigation done and found nothing,” he added.

what_happened: Deccan Herald reported that the Gujarat High Court issued notice to the Commission and the state on two petitions seeking a Special Investigation Team inquiry into Form 7 objections filed during the SIR. The Kodinar petition says about 47 people filed 6,722 applications, and the Sidhpur petitioners say one person filed about 140.
commission_reply: Deccan Herald reported that the matter was posted for further hearing on 7 July.

what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported Hyderabad's District Election Officer R. V. Karnan explaining that booth officers would hand out enumeration forms already printed with each elector's details and photograph, which the elector completes and signs.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; AIMIM; Booth level officers; Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana
what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Telangana BJP alleged to the Chief Electoral Officer that booth officers in Hyderabad were handing enumeration forms in bulk to AIMIM leaders at party camps and letting them upload filled forms. This is the BJP's allegation.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; Booth level officers; Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana
what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported that the BJP alleged that some booth officers in Serilingampally uploaded the blank back of enumeration forms to the Commission's app without the voter's details, and asked the Chief Electoral Officer for a probe. This is the BJP's allegation.

The Hindu reported that the Supreme Court agreed to consider an application by Congress MP Tanuj Punia alleging that Form 7 objections in the Uttar Pradesh SIR were filed with false particulars, forged signatures and in the names of people who later denied filing them. The application cited one person filing objections against 32 electors in Hata, Kushinagar, and a UP Congress claim of 700 to 800 objections in four Khalilabad booths.

The Pioneer reported that an Uttarakhand Congress delegation told the Chief Electoral Officer that one person had filed objections against about 6,400 voters and about 1,200 people had filed more than ten each. These are the Congress's figures.
commission_reply: The Pioneer reported that CEO V. V. R. C. Purushottam said the revision followed the rules and that observers had been sent to districts with many objections, and that Additional CEO Vijay Kumar Jogdande said an ERO must scrutinise cases where one person seeks the deletion of more than five names.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; Electoral Registration Officer; Election Commission
what_happened: Newslaundry reported that 35 people named as objectors on 1,657 Form 7s in Jhabrera, 31 of them BJP booth agents, said in affidavits that their names, EPIC numbers and signatures had been misused.
commission_reply: Newslaundry quoted the Jhabrera ERO saying the objections were cancelled after those named sought to withdraw them and the voters would not be deleted, and that the Election Commission would not order any investigation and those whose names were misused should file an FIR.

what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported, in a story datelined Hyderabad that does not say whether the figure covers the state or the district, that the Commission had received close to 50,000 Form 7 applications against entries in the draft roll, and that parties at a meeting chaired by Hyderabad's District Election Officer asked for the Form 10 lists by Assembly constituency.
commission_reply: Deccan Chronicle reported that officials gave parties the total number of applications at a meeting at the GHMC office but did not share figures by Assembly constituency.

what_happened: Newslaundry reported from its investigation in Uttarakhand that numerous applications were filed to delete Muslim voters' names from the rolls, many in the names of people it said were associated with the BJP. It reported that some people named as objectors later filed affidavits saying they had never filed the objections and that their names, EPIC numbers and signatures had been used fraudulently.

places: Karol Bagh; Patel Nagar; Sangam Vihar
what_happened: The Hindu reported that Form 10 lists published for 21 to 27 September showed four people in Delhi filing more than ten applications a day through the Commission's ECINET portal, which does not enforce the limit of ten a day for booth agents.
commission_reply: The Hindu reported that the office of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer did not respond to a request for comment.

parties_and_bodies: Congress; Civil society groups; Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka
what_happened: The Hindu reported that as of September 28, 4,000 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names had been filed in Karnataka, which it said mostly targeted Muslim voters. It reported that ten people filed Form 7s seeking deletion of 1,363 names in Babaleshwar in one day, often on forms with the voters' details already printed and only the objector's name handwritten. In Bhalki, it reported, 30 people filed Form 7s seeking deletion of 1,700 names. Civil society groups and the Karnataka Congress demanded that the Commission lodge criminal complaints.
commission_reply: V. Anbukumar, CEO, Karnataka, was not available for comment.

what_happened: Telangana Today reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, said 28,753 Form 7 applications had been filed in Telangana, about 5,000 of them in Hyderabad, and that forms received in bulk would be examined with special care.

parties_and_bodies: Congress; BJP; Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana
what_happened: Siasat reported that the Telangana Congress complained to the Chief Electoral Officer that a BJP booth agent in Musheerabad had filed Form 7 applications against a Congress booth agent and about 30 members of his family, on forms that were printed in advance. This is the Congress's allegation.
commission_reply: Siasat reported that the Congress asked for an investigation to establish the facts, including a forensic examination of whether the forms came from a common source.

what_happened: A BJP leader in Koppa, Chikkamagaluru, wrote on 1 October to withdraw Form 7 objections seeking the deletion of 243 voters filed on 21 and 22 September, saying the voters were found on re-verification to live within the polling stations' areas, Free Press Journal reported.
commission_reply: No response from the election authorities was reported.

what_happened: The New Indian Express reported that the Commission wrote to election officials in Bengaluru that bulk Form 7 applications had come to its notice, with allegations that some were not authentic. It reported that the Commission directed Electoral Registration Officers to act against applicants who knowingly make false declarations, after an inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

parties_and_bodies: Congress; BJP; Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana
what_happened: The South First reported that it had seen a Form 7 from a polling station in Aliyabad, in Bahadurpura, with the voter's details printed and the objector's part left blank. The Congress alleged that such forms had been handed to BJP booth agents through the party's constituency in-charges.
commission_reply: The South First reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, said at a press briefing that officials would thoroughly verify all Form 7 applications before making any decision.

what_happened: Of 13,443 Form 7 applications for deletion in Jharkhand, 4,790 came from the Chatra Assembly seat, about 36% of the state's total, in figures the Chief Electoral Officer released on 1 October, The Wire reported, citing the Hindustan Times. West Singhbhum had 1,906 and Deoghar 1,099.
commission_reply: The Wire reported that the Chief Electoral Officer said the Chatra figures were checked with the district administration and no bulk applications beyond the limit were found, and that address changes on Form 8 generate Form 7 entries automatically.

what_happened: Vartha Bharati reported, quoting the Chief Electoral Officer's office, that Karnataka received 8,85,952 Form 6, 4,648 Form 6A, 84,900 Form 7 and 11,78,028 Form 8 applications between 16 June and 1 October, and that 35,60,833 hearings had been held, with 7,82,304 pending.
commission_reply: The figures are a running count while hearings continue. Karnataka's final roll was published on 27 October 2026, and no count of the hearings' outcome came with it.

issues: Form 7; Pre-printed forms; Police and FIRs
what_happened: The News Minute reported that five FIRs were registered in Belagavi, Bidar and Mysuru over Form 7s alleged to carry false information or forged signatures, and that in Belagavi the voters' details had been filled in beforehand with the objector's name handwritten or blank. In Bidar the complaint alleged that 3,244 voters were falsely shown as shifted or absent, and an FIR naming 32 people was registered on 1 October.
commission_reply: The News Minute reported that Karnataka CEO V. Anbu Kumar said that although 84,900 Form 7s had been received, no one had been taken off the rolls.

parties_and_bodies: Congress; BJP; District Election Officer; Electoral Registration Officer
issues: Form 7; Pre-printed forms; Police and FIRs
what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported, citing Congress sources, that a BJP booth agent brought 15 pre-printed Form 7s to the booth officer at booth 173 in Goshamahal and that the booth officer refused to accept them.
commission_reply: Deccan Chronicle reported that the District Election Officer had reportedly directed the Musheerabad ERO to file criminal cases against the booth agent there.

what_happened: The News Minute reported that AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that Form 7s were being filed to have Muslim voters deleted and warned of protests, and that Congress leaders said the pre-printed forms found in Goshamahal and Bahadurpura were unsigned and were not accepted by booth officers.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; Police; Government of Karnataka; Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka
what_happened: The News Minute reported that Karnataka BJP leaders asked the state police chief to review the FIRs against party workers, saying filing several Form 7s is not by itself a crime and the rules set no limit on their number.
commission_reply: The News Minute reported that Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara said ministers had gone to the CEO's office to submit a memorandum.

parties_and_bodies: District Election Officer; BJP; Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana
what_happened: Siasat reported, citing PTI, that Hyderabad's District Election Officer R. V. Karnan said the Form 7s in Goshamahal and Musheerabad were not received in bulk and were rejected, the Goshamahal forms because they were unsigned and the Musheerabad ones because the electors were found living at the address.
commission_reply: Siasat reported that BJP state president N. Ramchander Rao said no BJP booth agents had submitted any such Form 7 applications, and that the Chief Electoral Officer had said bulk forms from a party had to be properly enquired into and verified.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana; District Election Officer; Electoral Registration Officer
what_happened: The News Minute quoted a memo of 5 October in which the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, told District Election Officers that bulk Form 7 applications had been filed and that EROs should act under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act against anyone who knowingly made a false declaration.
commission_reply: Siasat reported that the CEO said this action would follow an inquiry. The memo itself was not found on the CEO Telangana website.

issues: Form 7; Pre-printed forms; Police and FIRs
what_happened: The South First reported that the Telangana Congress asked the Hyderabad Police Commissioner to register an FIR and set up a Special Investigation Team over pre-filled Form 7s in three constituencies, and to examine the BJP's role. These are the Congress's allegations.
commission_reply: The South First reported that the Congress said the Police Commissioner had assured it he would study the matter and take action.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka; Electoral Registration Officer
what_happened: Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer said 91,278 Form 7 applications were received between 16 June and 4 October, that no name had yet been deleted because of one, and that each would go through a notice and hearing before an officer decided. He said EROs would inquire into bulk applications and that his office had registered no FIR, The News Minute reported.

Jayanagar police in Bengaluru registered an FIR against two BJP booth level agents and others on a complaint by Karnataka Mahila Congress president Sowmya Reddy, The Daily Jagran reported, carrying ANI. The complaint alleged Form 7 applications with forged signatures seeking to delete 5,698 voters by falsely claiming they had shifted.
commission_reply: No response from the BJP, the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission was reported.

what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported that Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that pre-printed Form 7s seeking the deletion of 122 electors, all Muslim, were submitted at booth 28 in Goshamahal in the name of a BJP supporter, and that the booth officer refused them. This is AIMIM's allegation.
commission_reply: Siasat reported on 5 October, citing PTI, that BJP state president N. Ramchander Rao said no BJP booth agents had submitted any such Form 7 applications.

issues: Form 7; Pre-printed forms; Police and FIRs
what_happened: Telangana Today reported that Chikkadpally police were checking the forms, signatures and voter details in the Musheerabad case and whether similar forms were filed elsewhere, and that the forms had reportedly been rejected.

A Judicial Magistrate First Class in Haldwani ordered the Banbhoolpura police on 6 October to register an FIR and investigate. A booth agent of a party had said that Form 7s seeking to delete 28 voters in part 134 were filed online in his name without his knowledge, and the court held that tracing who filed them needed a police investigation, Haldwani Express News reported.
commission_reply: Haldwani Express News reported that the police had told the court the complaint concerned SIR Form 7s and that the complainant could object before the assistant returning officer.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; JD(S); Governor of Karnataka; Government of Karnataka; Police
what_happened: A BJP and JD(S) delegation including Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy and R Ashoka asked Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot to direct the state government to stop registering criminal cases against people who filed Form 7 objections, ThePrint reported, carrying PTI. They alleged police were being misused to intimidate BJP workers and that the Chief Electoral Office had given in to the state government.
commission_reply: No response from the state government, the Chief Electoral Officer or Congress was reported.

parties_and_bodies: Congress; BJP; JD(S); Booth level officers
what_happened: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar alleged on 6 October that BJP and JD(S) workers had filed Form 7 applications in bulk and then collected back and destroyed more than a lakh of them, threatening booth officers, The News Minute reported. This is his allegation.
commission_reply: BJP MLC C T Ravi asked the Commission to register a case against people making baseless allegations and sought legal action against Shivakumar.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; Police; BJP; Congress
issues: Form 7; Pre-printed forms; Police and FIRs
what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Musheerabad ERO filed a police complaint, and Chikkadpally police registered a case, against a BJP booth agent who tried to submit 30 pre-printed Form 7s, the first such case in Telangana.
commission_reply: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Congress welcomed the case and asked the police to find who printed and supplied the forms.

what_happened: A BJP and JD(S) delegation led by Jayanagar MLA C K Ramamurthy went to Jayanagar police station in Bengaluru and demanded that the FIR against BJP workers over Form 7 applications be withdrawn, IANS reported. They warned of an intensified agitation if it was not, and alleged that applications meant to be confidential had been handed to Congress workers.
commission_reply: No police response was reported.

what_happened: Police at Shanivarasanthe in Kodagu district registered a case against five BJP booth level workers on a complaint that they sought the deletion of 64 voters in Byadagutta village through Form 7 applications, IANS reported.

The Wire reported, citing The Hindu's analysis of Delhi's constituency data, that 569 Form 6 applications and 3,209 Form 7 applications were disposed of between 31 August and 4 October, about six Form 7s for every Form 6. It said 2,352 of the Form 7s were disposed of in the last two weeks, and that 2.12 lakh Form 6 and 51,747 Form 7 applications had been submitted from 16 June, before the claims period began on 31 August.
commission_reply: No response from the Chief Electoral Officer was reported. On 22 October the Chief Electoral Officer's office replaced the weekly disposal report on which this analysis rests, and officials said the earlier figures were wrong. The revised figures are entered separately, from The Hindu of 23 October.

issues: Form 7; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: Data released by Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer on 8 October showed 24,323 Form 7 applications received from 15 June to 7 October and 12,204 names deleted, PTI reported. The figure is lower than the 28,753 Form 7s the CEO said on 1 October had been filed, and the reports do not explain the difference.
commission_reply: State BJP president N Ramchander Rao said the Commission decides deletions only after field inquiries.

what_happened: The Karnataka High Court at Dharwad told the police on 8 October to take no coercive steps until 13 October against a BJP functionary and two supporters booked over Form 7s against voters in Belagavi, LiveLaw and Bar and Bench reported. A Congress block agent's complaint, as the police record it, alleges they handed about 198 fabricated Form 7s to the booth officer. On 13 October Justice Venkatesh Naik T stayed the investigation until the next hearing, citing a coordinate bench's stay in similar cases on 9 October, Bar and Bench reported. The Court allowed the State to seek to have the order modified or vacated, and posted the matter for 29 October.
commission_reply: The Government Pleader sought time to file objections and the latest investigation report.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi; Electoral Registration Officer
what_happened: Delhi Chief Electoral Officer Ashok Kumar announced on 9 October that the Commission had decided to limit an individual voter to ten Form 7 objections for the whole claims and objections period and five a month during continuous updation, citing bulk objections on unsubstantiated grounds, IANS reported. The statement said registration officers would act against false objections under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

The Karnataka High Court stayed proceedings in two FIRs against two BJP booth agents accused over bulk Form 7s against voters in Bengaluru's Malleshwaram constituency, Bar and Bench reported. The judge said the FIRs looked premature because the registration officer had not yet decided the Form 7s. One FIR concerns applications against 778 voters in ward 64 and the other objections against 136 voters in ward 45.
commission_reply: The State said the allegations of impersonation and forgery needed investigation and that the agents filed more applications than allowed. The complainant's counsel said the bulk filing was a conspiracy aimed at OBC and SC/ST voters.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh; Election Commission
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that in the Tarabganj and Pilibhit Assembly constituencies 90 per cent of Form 7 deletion requests were against Muslim voters, and that in Tarabganj 188 objections were filed under one name on the same date against voters of one booth. It said the published data give no identity of an objector beyond a name, so the objectors cannot be checked.
commission_reply: The Collective said it sent questions to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission and had no reply by publication. The report does not say how it determined the voters' religion.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral registration officers; Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, Andhra Pradesh
what_happened: The News Minute found that 40,006 electors were named for deletion in Form 7 applications in Andhra Pradesh between 29 September and 10 October, the last 12 days of claims and objections, and that 20,959 of them had an Electoral Registration Officer or an Assistant Electoral Registration Officer named as the objector in the Commission's consolidated Form 10 statements. Where an ordinary elector is the objector the statements give a reason, and where an officer is named they give none. In the 20 constituencies with the most names sought for deletion, officers were the objectors for 16,241 of 21,115. In Chandragiri the assistant officer is named 1,991 times and the officer 6 times among 2,452 names, in Palacole the officer 311 times and the assistant officer 1,701 times among 2,220, in Ongole the officer 1,277 times among 1,712, and in Narsapuram 1,369 times among 1,450. TNM could not read the statements from before 29 September, because each stays online for a week. The report sets out that rule 13(2) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 lets only an elector on the roll object to an entry, and that section 22 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and rule 21A let the officer delete a name of his own motion after giving the elector a chance to be heard. Two registration officers told TNM that the ERO-NET software is built so that the reason does not show, and one of them said that it allows deletions to be uploaded in bulk. An assistant registration officer said the only option in his login is to mark an elector ineligible, which generates the Form 7, and that the reason is then not listed.
commission_reply: TNM sent questions to Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Vivek Yadav, and had no reply when it published. The Chief Electoral Officer answered on 28 October that the forms were generated through the software on the Commission's instructions for electors found ineligible after notices (form7-65). One registration officer told TNM that the officer is never in fact the objector, that the request comes from a family member or a booth level agent, and that his office holds documents to show it.

issues: Form 7; Software (ECINET/ERONET); Names left off or deleted
what_happened: Several State election officials told The Hindu that the Commission's software, ERONet, generated Form 7s automatically when officials deleted electors at the hearings of the revision, and that the forms carried the officers' digital signatures, the paper reported on 15 October. It named Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal as states where officials had used this route to delete electors with unresolved logical discrepancies or with no mapping, and it said other reports had put the names deleted this way at more than 87,000 in Uttar Pradesh and more than 95,000 in Uttarakhand. The paper reported, from sources, that no written communication or standard operating procedure on these forms was shared with the election authorities in the states. It set out that the electoral rules make no provision for a registration officer or an assistant registration officer to file a Form 7, and that the Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2024 makes none for the registration officer to file one, though the officer, who decides objections, can delete a name found ineligible. The paper reports that the manual mentions auto-generated Form 7s only in the verification of Photo Similar Entries, where the forms ERONet generates are not filed by the registration officer and must be signed by the booth level officer after a field verification, or the system cannot accept or process them.
