commission_reply: The paper reported that the Commission had yet to answer an official query on the matter. Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer said on 28 October that the forms in that state were generated through ECINET in the officers' names as the Commission instructs, for electors found ineligible after a notice and a speaking order (form7-65). Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer's office called the account of such forms in that state misleading on 13 October, and said notices, hearings, scrutiny and recorded orders came before any action (up-02).

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal; BJP; Trinamool Congress
what_happened: The Wire reported that on 16 January 2026, during West Bengal's extended claims period, the Commission told the state's Chief Electoral Officer in writing that the law set no limit on the number of Form 7 objections one voter could file, and that on 9 October it capped them at ten per voter for a whole claims period, in an instruction to every state. The October instruction cites a paragraph of the Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023 against entertaining objections presented in bulk by an individual, which the January letter did not mention. Reading the Chief Electoral Officer's daily bulletins, the report counts 3,143 objections from party agents by 20 January, 2,926 from BJP agents and 217 from Trinamool agents, and finds that 2,539 of them first appear in the bulletin dated the day after the extended window closed on 19 January.
commission_reply: The report says the Commission has not said whether objections filed in January will be looked at again.

what_happened: The Wire reported, citing The Hindu, that 4,263 of the 13,462 Form 7 applications Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer received between 31 August and 16 October, or 31.67%, had not been published in the Form 10 lists. The Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023 requires each objection to be listed publicly for seven days before an Electoral Registration Officer can act on it.
commission_reply: The Hindu reported that it sent questions to the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office and had no response by the time of publication.

what_happened: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer replaced the weekly report of applications disposed of on 22 October, and officials told The Hindu that the figures published until then were wrong. The revised report shows 1,07,451 of 4,59,796 Form 6 applications for inclusion and 47,105 of 67,709 Form 7 applications disposed of from 31 August to 18 October, about 23% and 70%. The earlier report had shown 1,238 Form 6 disposals to 11 October. Tri Nagar is the only constituency with no Form 6 disposal recorded in any of the seven weeks.
commission_reply: The Hindu attributes the quoted explanation to an unnamed official and does not say which office the official works in. More than 3.5 lakh Form 6 applications were still to be disposed of. Claims close on 30 October, every application is to be disposed of by 30 November, and the final roll is due on 4 December.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka; Congress; BJP
what_happened: Karnataka received 2,28,917 Form 7 applications between 16 June and 22 October, 1,70,442 of them after 23 September, when the count stood at 58,475, The Indian Express reported from official data. The Chief Electoral Officer's office said every Form 7 received up to 23 September had been cleared on priority and that hearings for all 43.82 lakh voters sent notices were over. Bangalore Urban had the most submissions in the paper's table, 24,268. The ruling Congress has alleged that the BJP is misusing Form 7 to file objections in bulk.
commission_reply: After a Congress protest at the Chief Electoral Officer's office earlier this month, the Chief Electoral Officer directed Electoral Registration Officers to look into the allegations. The state BJP has rejected them. The final roll is due on 27 October.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; Electoral Registration Officer; Election Commission; Congress
issues: Form 7; Names left off or deleted; Minorities
what_happened: Newslaundry found 4,390 names on Kichha's draft roll that are missing from the final roll published on 3 October. About 670 of them had Form 7 objections filed against them in August, 509 by a single BJP booth level agent, and the other 3,720 had no objection against them and were deleted on the ground of logical discrepancies. Of the 6,884 Form 7 objections accepted in Kichha, 5,359 were that agent's, and he filed more Form 7 objections than anyone else in Uttarakhand. He told Newslaundry that the Electoral Registration Officer at first refused his bulk objections and took them after he complained to the Election Commission by email, and Newslaundry could not verify what the email said. Form 10 data from the Chief Electoral Officer's office show 504 of his accepted objections with an acceptance date of 14 August, a day after claims and objections closed. Newslaundry reported that every name in his objections was Muslim. He said the party had received information that about 6,000 electors enrolled in Kichha were also enrolled in five nearby constituencies of Uttar Pradesh.
commission_reply: The Kichha Electoral Registration Officer, Gaurav Pandey, neither confirmed nor denied the agent's account, would not say whether the Commission had directed him, and said the deletions followed the Commission's rules. Newslaundry said the Commission acknowledged its questions and did not answer them, and that it had asked the Chief Electoral Officer why objections were accepted after the deadline. The Congress MLA for Kichha, Tilak Raj Behar, said the objections rested on false information. The report does not say how it established the electors' religion.

what_happened: The Dharavi police registered a case under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 against a resident who had submitted 24 Form 7 applications in one day in the 178-Dharavi constituency, above the Election Commission's limit of ten a day, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation said on 24 October, The Hindu reported. The corporation alleged that the applications carried false and incorrect information. Mumbai's draft rolls were published on 31 August and claims and objections ran to 26 October.
commission_reply: The report gives no account from the accused. Section 31 covers anyone who knowingly makes a false statement or declaration in connection with the roll.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh; Booth level officers; Samajwadi Party; Police
issues: Form 7; Police and FIRs; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: A first information report was registered on 24 October against unknown persons, under sections 318(4), 336(3) and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for cheating and forgery, over Form 7 applications that sought the deletion of 26 electors at booth 96 in the Sultanpur Sadar constituency, The Wire reported. The forms were presented as signed by an elector who has said publicly that he cannot read or write and uses his thumbprint. The complaint was made by the lekhpal who supervises the booth, and it does not say who submitted the forms. The Samajwadi Party raised the case in February (up-10), and its president Akhilesh Yadav presented the elector to the media in Lucknow on 8 February.
commission_reply: Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa said on 26 October that the report of the District Election Officer of Sultanpur found the forms had been given to the booth level officer, and that no action was taken on them because they did not carry the applicant's full name, EPIC number or mobile number. He said the booth level officer had been relieved of all election work and that disciplinary action had been recommended.

issues: Form 7; Notices and hearings; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: At least 61,059 Form 7 applications seeking deletions from Karnataka's rolls were filed by Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers themselves, and none gives a reason for the deletion, which the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 require, The Hindu reported. Officers listed as the objectors said the system generated the forms with their digital signatures when electors sent notices for no mapping or logical discrepancies could not be reached at hearings and were marked ineligible. Only 192 such applications were filed between 24 August and 23 September, and more than 60,800 between 24 September and 22 October, including 10,105 on 22 October, the last day for disposal. The paper's chart puts more than 53,000 of the officers' applications in the week from 16 to 22 October, with the most on one day, 11,760, on 19 October. In every case the paper checked on the Commission's portal the elector had already been deleted, including electors against whom the application came after 23 September. In the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike South district officers filed 10,374 of 17,491 applications, and in at least 26 constituencies officers filed more than voters or third parties did.
commission_reply: The officers said they had been told to file Form 7 for electors who had shifted, had a duplicate entry, were underage, had died or were not citizens. The report gives no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer. Rule 17 of the 1960 Rules says a claim or objection not lodged within the period or in the prescribed form and manner shall be rejected by the registration officer. The paper also found 13,808 fewer Form 7 applications for 24 September to 22 October in the Commission's Form 10 records than the Chief Electoral Officer's statements give.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Andhra Pradesh; Electoral registration officers; Election Commission
what_happened: Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer answered TNM's report on Form 7s naming officers as objectors (form7-64) on 28 October, in a thread on the office's X account that says no registration officer or assistant registration officer deleted any name of his own motion. The thread says booth level officers found 44,89,512 electors not at their addresses between 15 June and 24 July 2026, and the draft roll of 31 July held 3,71,38,182 electors. Officers then sent notices to electors with no mapping or with data anomalies, and by 23 October another 1,73,701 electors had been found ineligible for the final roll. For each of them, the thread says, the officer passed a speaking order giving the reasons and uploaded it to ECINET, the booth level officer delivered the order to the elector with notice of an appeal to the District Collector, and a Form 7 was generated through ECINET in the officer's name as the Commission instructs, because a deletion takes effect in the system only after a Form 7 is generated. It calls the report's insinuations of procedural violations baseless and misleading and condemns them. The News Minute replied the same day that the statement does not say why officers appear as objectors in the published records or why no reason is shown in those cases.
commission_reply: The thread is the Chief Electoral Officer's own reply. TNM says its report did not allege that officers deleted names without due process, and that its question was why the public records give no reason for the deletions officers are named in. The thread does not say how many of the 20,959 electors in TNM's count are among the 1,73,701.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana; Election Commission
what_happened: From 1 January to 14 June 2026, before the revision began in Telangana, 5,13,375 Form 7 applications were filed and 4,54,340 accepted, The Hindu reported from information shared by the Chief Electoral Officer's office. In all since 1 January, 5,81,273 Form 7 applications were filed, 5,08,057 accepted, 54,681 rejected and 18,535 were under process, a count that includes electors found ineligible for the final roll at the notice stage. Of 10,77,450 Form 6 applications received from 1 January to 28 October, 2,43,643 were rejected, about 23%, and 1,61,214 were pending, and 1,92,574 of the 5,20,331 received before the revision were rejected, 37%. Only 1,70,374 Form 6 applications came in during claims and objections, which ended on 7 October. The paper puts 73,39,235 electors left off the draft at enumeration and says the exclusions from the roll could be well over 80 lakh.
commission_reply: Officials said the Form 7 deletions before the revision were entries sifted by an application on the ECINET software as Demographically Similar Entries and Photo Similar Entries. The paper says no explanation was given for the 47,303 Form 7 applications rejected in the same period.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; District Election Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi; Congress
what_happened: The office of the North East Delhi District Election Officer, Ajay Kumar, said on 31 October that election officers would visit every elector against whom a Form 7 objection had been filed in the Mustafabad constituency to check the claim before any name is deleted, and that it would act under the rules against objectors whose claims were found false or mischievous, The Hindu reported. The office was replying to a post on X that shared the paper's report of 30 October, which found all 28 electors at polling booth 129 against whom a booth level agent appointed by the BJP had filed objections, citing absence, a permanent shift or death, living at their registered addresses. The paper reported 843 Form 7 applications in the constituency by 28 October, and 572 of them filed by 19 of the BJP's booth level agents, all against Muslim electors, in 24 parts of the constituency. With 118 more filed on 29 and 30 October the total reached 961, and 684 of them, 71%, were filed by the BJP's agents, the paper reported from the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's list of applications. Officials told the paper the agents' applications carried no undertaking from the agent and were not in the prescribed format. Nine more applications naming the agent at booth 129 as objector appeared on the list of 30 October.
commission_reply: The District Election Officer's office said no bulk applications beyond the prescribed limits had been received in Mustafabad, online or on paper, and gave a figure of 832 Forms 7 and 8, 102 of them Form 8, filed in the constituency up to 30 October, which differs from the public list. Senior officials of the Commission told the paper that agents who file as objectors without the undertaking for bulk filing are held to the limit of ten applications set on 9 October. The agent named at booth 129 had told the paper he did not file the forms and was neither a booth level agent nor associated with any party. Neither report says how the paper established that the electors were Muslim. Ali Mehdi, the Congress candidate for Mustafabad in the 2025 Assembly election, said in a post on X that he had complained to the North East Delhi Deputy Commissioner of Police and sought an FIR against the BJP's agents.

what_happened: Figures generated by the Telangana Chief Electoral Officer's office show 50,908 Form 7 applications filed from 8 to 31 October, after claims and objections closed on 7 October, with 48,623 accepted and 435 rejected, Telangana Today reported. State election officials told the paper that a glitch in generating the data had brought some earlier applications into these figures. The Hindu had reported on 29 October, from official records, 5,81,273 Form 7 applications filed in the state since 1 January, which is 7,386 fewer than this report's total of 5,88,659 to 31 October. By the same figures Rangareddy district had 11,935 applications, of which 11,378 were accepted. Hyderabad had 9,858, of which 9,616 were accepted and four rejected, and Medchal Malkajgiri 4,018, of which 3,783 were accepted and four rejected. During claims and objections, from 17 August to 7 October, 15,442 Form 7 applications were filed, 12,930 accepted and 1,637 rejected. From 1 January to 31 October, 5,88,659 Form 7 applications were recorded, 5,16,052 accepted, 57,980 rejected and 14,627 pending.
commission_reply: State election officials told the paper that a registration officer must give a speaking order with reasons before a name is deleted, and that they were trying to include as many electors as possible in the final roll. The paper says senior officials of the Chief Electoral Officer's office could not explain the number filed after the claims period.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral registration officers; Chief Electoral Officer, Uttarakhand; BJP
issues: Form 7; Schedule and deadlines; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: Form 10 records published by Uttarakhand's Chief Electoral Officer show that Gadarpur's Electoral Registration Officer and ten Assistant Electoral Registration Officers filed 2,742 Form 7 objections on two dates, 763 on 18 September and 1,979 on 28 September, Newslaundry reported on 2 November. Claims and objections had closed on 13 August, and the final roll was published on 3 October. Rule 17 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 requires an objection lodged after the period to be rejected. By the same records, objections against 4,785 names were filed by 13 August and against 2,825 after it, and the other 83 late objections were filed by individuals, 27 of them dated 14 August by a BJP leader. Of the 5,505 names deleted in Gadarpur after the draft, 2,496 followed objections by the assistant registration officers, 240 objections by the registration officer and 240 objections by private persons, and 2,529 were deleted with no objection recorded against them. Newslaundry met at least 15 deleted electors who said they learnt of it only after the final roll was published. Some said they had received a notice and others that they had received none, and all said officials told them to file Form 6 again. The registration officer, Amrita Sharma, told Newslaundry that officers had not known a Form 7 also had to be generated for electors marked absent, and that by the time this was noticed the hearings were over.
commission_reply: The registration officer said the late filings were a delay in generating the forms on the system, that hearings had already been held, and that these were Form 7 deletions on anomaly notices, which she distinguished from an officer's own proceedings under rule 21A. She said about 52,000 notices were issued in Gadarpur and about 45,000 electors heard and kept on the roll, that not a single name was deleted without a notice, and that the same ten assistant officers who filed the objections held the hearings. She said only forms submitted by 13 August were accepted and that the entries dated 14 August were uploads made late that night. On two electors who say they gave the documents asked for or had no notice, she said she would have to examine the records. She said more than 1,800 Form 6 applications had been received since the revision, over 900 of them from electors deleted for absence or other reasons. The report gives no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; Electoral Registration Officer; District Election Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi; Election Commission
issues: Form 7; Minorities; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: Twenty people registered with the Election Commission as the BJP's booth level agents are named as objectors in 787 Form 7 applications in Delhi's Mustafabad constituency, at least 77% of the 1,021 deletion applications filed there so far, The Hindu reported on 4 November from the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's public list. The paper reports that all 787 are against Muslim electors and that they are 94% of the 837 deletion applications filed by third parties. It contacted all 20 agents, and 16 of them denied filing or signing any of the forms. One agent named in 32 applications told the paper he had complained to the party and resigned as its agent, and the paper reports that it checked with the area's booth level officer that the electors in those applications live at their registered addresses. One agent named in 57 applications said he had filed them and put his own total at 500 forms. Two agents could not be reached, and the number listed for another was a wrong number. The forms naming the 20 agents were filed without the undertaking or the format prescribed for an agent's bulk filing, the paper has learnt, and all of them were received after the Commission set a limit of ten Form 7 applications for each elector on 9 October. An agent named in 56 applications said the Electoral Registration Officer's office called him on 3 November about the objections and that he told it he had not filed them.
commission_reply: The District Election Officer, the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission did not answer the paper's questions. The District Election Officer had said earlier that every deletion claim would be verified in person by the booth level officer and the registration officer or an assistant, and that action would be taken against claims found false or mischievous (form7-58). The Commission's directive of 9 October, as the paper quotes it, says a registration officer who finds a Form 7 complaint false or fabricated shall act against the applicant under the Representation of the People Act. The report does not say how the paper established that the electors were Muslim.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi; BJP
issues: Form 7; Police and FIRs; Transparency of lists
source: Anjali Bhardwaj on X, posting the petitioners' letter of 5 November 2026 to the Chief Election Commissioner, the two Election Commissioners and Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer
what_happened: Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, the petitioners in the Supreme Court case on Delhi's revision (W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, court-54), wrote on 5 November 2026 to the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, the Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, and Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer, Ashok Kumar, about The Hindu's report on Form 7 applications in Mustafabad (form7-60). Their letter gives the report's figures, that at least 787 of the 1,021 deletion applications filed there were in the names of 20 booth level agents appointed by the BJP, all against Muslim electors, and that 16 of the 20 denied filling, signing or knowing of the forms. The letter says this indicates that their identities appear to have been forged and used fraudulently without their consent. It asks the Commission and the Chief Electoral Officer to direct the registration of FIRs under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including for forgery, criminal impersonation, identity fraud and false declarations, and to audit every Form 7 submitted in every Delhi constituency during the revision to check whether the objectors named authorised and signed them. After investigation, it asks for action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 against everyone who knowingly made a false or fabricated declaration in a Form 7. It asks for an immediate stay on every deletion arising from a third-party Form 7 until the electors concerned and the objectors named have been independently verified. It also asks for a public report of how many Form 7 applications were received, how many were confirmed on verification and how many were found to be fraudulent, and for every Form 7 received during the revision to be published on the Chief Electoral Officer's website so that people can check whether one was filed in their name.
commission_reply: No reply from the Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer had been reported by 5 November. The Commission's directive of 9 October, as The Hindu quotes it, says a registration officer who finds a Form 7 complaint false or fabricated shall act against the applicant under the Representation of the People Act (form7-60). The North East Delhi District Election Officer had said on 31 October that every Form 7 in Mustafabad would be verified in the field before any name is deleted (form7-58).

parties_and_bodies: BJP; Electoral Registration Officer; District Election Officer; Police; Congress
what_happened: The Electoral Registration Officer of Delhi's Mustafabad constituency lodged a police complaint on Friday 6 November seeking an FIR under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, against a booth level agent named as objector on 37 Form 7 applications, The Hindu reported. The North East Delhi District Election Officer, Ajay Kumar, told the paper that officials had verified its report of 30 October on polling part 129 (form7-58) and found 36 of the 37 forms false or fabricated. A press release from his office said that the booth level officer and the assistant registration officer had checked all 37, that three electors the forms gave as dead were found alive, and that the others were found living at their addresses. It said that verification of the other Form 7 applications was continuing. The paper's earlier report had found the agent registered with the BJP by the Commission's records. A senior police officer told Daijiworld that the complaint had been received and that an investigation was under way. The Delhi Congress leader Ali Mehdi told Daijiworld that he had complained on 31 October, naming 14 booth level agents, and handed a copy to the Chief Electoral Officer, and that the matter was formally registered only a week later.
commission_reply: The Delhi BJP spokesperson, Praveen Shankar Kapoor, told Daijiworld that the party had not submitted any such forms, and that the booth level officer is responsible for checking every Form 7 before a name is deleted. The agent had told The Hindu earlier that he did not file the forms and was neither a booth level agent nor associated with any party (form7-58). The reports give no FIR number and do not say whether an FIR has been registered.

issues: Form 7; Minorities; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: The 796 Form 7 applications that name 20 booth level agents appointed by the BJP as objectors in Delhi's Mustafabad constituency are mostly concentrated in 25 of its 294 polling booths, in the neighbourhoods of Nehru Vihar, Dayalpur and Chandu Nagar, The Hindu reported on 10 November. The paper reports that all of them are against Muslim electors and that they are over 76% of the 1,044 deletion applications received in the constituency up to 4 November, from the published data. The applications give absence, a permanent shift or death as the reason, and the paper found at least 87 of the electors named living at their registered addresses. The paper reports, from an analysis of records and interviews with local BJP workers, that the 25 booths appeared to have been selected because they had a sizeable Muslim population and, by the workers' claims, few names left off the draft roll. BJP leaders who spoke to it on condition of anonymity said that after the draft of 31 August party workers compared the number of names placed on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors in booths with a majority of Muslim electors and in booths with a majority of Hindu electors, prepared lists of Muslim electors, which the paper says it saw, and then concentrated on the 25 booths, where the agents began filing from the first week of October. The paper says it found copies of these booths' rolls, with the names of Muslim electors marked on them, with BJP workers in the area. It reports that the Commission's booth-wise figures do not bear out the workers' claim. By its count, names left off the draft averaged 274 a booth in Mustafabad and reached 538 at the most, and in most of the 25 booths they were close to the average. Parts 108 and 129, which it counts among the five booths with the fewest names left off the draft, carry 35 and 37 of the agents' applications. No application names a BJP agent in the other three, which BJP workers said were mostly Hindu. Nehru Vihar has the most applications, 496. The paper reports that none of the Form 7s received in Mustafabad came with the undertaking an agent must give.
commission_reply: The Delhi BJP spokesperson, Praveen Shankar Kapoor, told the paper that the party's agents had not filed any Form 7s in Mustafabad, that the party had not directed any forms to be filed, and that booth level officers and the Commission would act on any objections under the rules. The BJP councillor for Nehru Vihar, Arun Bhati, said he was not authorised to speak about the applications, and said that some booths in Mustafabad had 300 to 500 votes deleted, which he said were coincidentally of Hindu voters, while others had fewer than 100, and that the two could not both be correct. The paper reports that officials maintain religious identity has no role in verification. The agent named in 57 applications told the paper he had filed them himself because the electors had shifted, and the councillor's brother, an agent named in 37, denied filing his. The report does not say how the paper established the religion of the electors or of each booth's population.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Maharashtra; BJP; Samajwadi Party
what_happened: Amit Sanap, the electoral registration officer for Bhiwandi East, told the Hindustan Times that his office had received 540 Form 7 applications seeking deletions in the constituency and had rejected over 450 of them, because the electors the forms said were not living at their addresses were found living there. The paper reports that political parties' booth level agents filed 480 of the 540 and that some applicants could face criminal action for false information. Sanap said some applicants had withdrawn their applications and that action would begin once the formal orders were prepared. The paper reports that Form 7s filed by agents and private complainants have been withdrawn or rejected in large numbers on scrutiny in Mumbai and the constituencies around it, after Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer told registration officers to place the burden of proof on the objector, to summon objectors and verify their claims before acting, and to begin criminal action against false filings. A senior state election official told the paper that objectors are allowed to withdraw, and that withdrawals began once action started and the first FIR was registered in Dharavi three weeks earlier (form7-55). With claims and objections due to close on Friday, 13 November, the Commission had received over 23 lakh forms for additions, deletions and corrections in Maharashtra, more than 95,000 of them Form 7s, the paper reports.
commission_reply: Rais Shaikh, the Samajwadi Party MLA for Bhiwandi East, alleged that agents of the BJP had filed objections in bulk against his party's supporters and withdrew them only when faced with police action. The BJP's Atul Deulgaonkar, who oversees the revision for the party, rejected the allegations of the Samajwadi Party and the Congress and said electors of opposition parties were not being targeted. He said anyone with credible information about an incorrect registration has the right to file a Form 7 and that the authorised officer decides whether it is correct. The report does not say which parties' agents filed the 480 applications in Bhiwandi East.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi; Election Commission; Booth level officers
what_happened: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer's office received 3,04,352 Form 6 applications for inclusion, 549 Form 6A applications, 30,954 Form 7 objections seeking deletion and 1,11,516 Form 8 applications for correction or shifting between the draft of 31 August and 11 November, according to the bulletin it issued on 12 November, Hindustan Times reported. The paper gives the totals with the applications received before the draft as 5,16,752 Form 6, 1,900 Form 6A, 82,425 Form 7 and 3,72,284 Form 8. Claims and objections close on 25 November, the applications are to be disposed of by 15 December and the final roll is due on 22 December. Hindustan Times reported that the enumeration forms for electors left off the draft had not yet begun to be handed out, and an official told the paper that this would begin the next week because the ECINet software was being updated. The paper reports that each booth level officer will have to reach about 300 such electors. PTI reported officials as saying that the Commission was changing the portal so that booth level officers could generate forms only for the electors left off, and an official of the Commission as saying that at present forms are generated for all 1.45 crore electors in Delhi and the officers have to pick out those left off by hand. The official told Hindustan Times that the office would review whether the schedule needs a further extension, next week or closer to 25 November. The Tribune reported, from officials, that the Commission is considering an extension of about two weeks, which is yet to be approved and is to be discussed at the next meeting, and that nearly 15,000 booth level officers are expected to visit the registered addresses of the electors left off and hand them fresh forms.
commission_reply: None of the officials is named in the three reports, and none of the reports says that an extension has been ordered. Officials told The Tribune that electors who have already filed Form 6 during the revision need not file an enumeration form and that their applications will be decided by the registration officers. The Commission's letter of 6 November says that such an elector need not submit the enumeration form and that the application is to be decided under its letter of 3 November. The letter sets no last date for the enumeration forms.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Maharashtra; Election Commission
what_happened: Maharashtra received 23,60,021 applications for inclusion, deletion and correction on its electoral roll in its 36 districts from the draft of 31 August to 12 November, the day before claims and objections closed, The Times of India reported on 14 November from the district figures released by the state election office. The paper reports that 15.18 lakh of them were Form 6 applications for inclusion, 1.25 lakh were Form 7 applications seeking deletion and 7,15,729 were Form 8 applications for correction. Hindustan Times, reporting the same figures on 14 November, gives 1,25,693 Form 7 applications. Mumbai Suburban received the most applications, 1,91,308, followed by Pune with 1,65,446 and Thane with 1,64,834, and Sindhudurg received the fewest, 16,098. Election officials told The Times of India that the count includes only the applications made online and that the forms submitted on paper had not yet been digitised. The paper reports that the district figures also leave out the applications received on 13 November, the last day, and officials told it that the final count will therefore be higher. The paper reports that the applications are to be disposed of by 25 November and that the final roll is to be published on 30 November.
commission_reply: The Times of India reports that the Commission had not announced any further extension of the period for claims and objections when the paper went to press, although opposition parties and activists had asked for one. They argued that the period was too short because it took in the Diwali week, and that electors whose names were left off the draft would need time to submit documents. The report names no official.

places: Nandurbar; Nanded; Jalna; Mumbai; Thane; Pune
parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Maharashtra; Election Commission; Booth level officers
issues: Notices and hearings; Documents and declaration
what_happened: Of the 12.24 million electors on Maharashtra's draft roll who were served notices, 6.25 million for discrepancies in their names, ages, addresses and other details and 5.98 million because they could not be mapped to the 2002 roll, 99.41 per cent have cleared and 72,601 have not, because they have yet to submit documents or their documents are still being checked, Hindustan Times reported on 14 November. The Times of India reported the same day, from the latest data released by election officials, that 99.4 per cent of the 1.2 crore electors served notices had cleared scrutiny and would stay on the roll. It gives 99.6 per cent of the 62.5 lakh served notices for discrepancies and 99.2 per cent of the 59.7 lakh served notices as unmapped. An official of the Chief Electoral Officer's office told Hindustan Times that documents can be submitted and verified until 23 November and that a few more of these electors are expected to clear. Both papers report that Nandurbar has the highest share cleared, 99.99 per cent, and Nanded the lowest, 96.18 per cent, followed by Jalna at 96.83 per cent. Both give Mumbai City at 99.61 per cent, Mumbai Suburban at 99.73 per cent and Thane at 99.88 per cent, and The Times of India gives Pune at 98.91 per cent. Hindustan Times reports that so many cleared after the Commission relaxed its guidelines for the revision in Maharashtra and other states. By its account, personal hearings with booth level officers were dropped, documents could be sent on WhatsApp and PAN and Aadhaar details were accepted. Election officers at the assembly constituency level told the paper that after the protests across the country booth level officers were told to be lenient and could decide for themselves whether to ask an elector for more details.
commission_reply: None of the officials is named in either report. A senior official of the Chief Electoral Officer's office told The Times of India that the figure showed that in 99.4 per cent of cases the documents and information supplied by the electors served notices were found satisfactory. Neither report gives a response from a political party, and neither says what will happen to the 72,601 electors whose cases are not settled by 23 November.

what_happened: The Commission announced in May 2025 that it was building ECINET, one platform to bring together more than 40 of its apps and websites for voters, election officials and other users.
The Supreme Court recorded, from the documents before it, what the logical discrepancy category in West Bengal covered and that about 1.36 crore voters fell in it.
The Commission launched ECINET formally on 22 January 2026 and said its trial version had already been used during the Bihar election and the SIR.
Meghalaya's Chief Electoral Officer listed six checks that ECINET used to flag mapping discrepancies in the third phase, among them a sibling age gap under nine months.

After its full meeting on 26 September 2026 the Commission said field officers have access to ECINET by role, set up a committee with an independent expert to check ECINET against the law, and said new IT modules would first go to a committee of officers.
Booth officers in Bhopal told the Free Press Journal they were asked to upload 100 forms a day and could not, because the booth officers' app server was down or very slow.

issues: Notices and hearings; Software (ECINET/ERONET); Transparency of lists
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported, from internal Commission records it acquired, that the Commission's software initially flagged 1.31 crore voters in West Bengal and 2.35 crore in Madhya Pradesh for logical discrepancies, and that officials had no written instructions on how to resolve them. It reported that no criteria for deciding which flagged voters to summon had been made public.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Commission did not answer its question on how flagged voters were chosen, and that questions sent to the Commission and three state offices on testing and procedure went unanswered.

what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that on 29 December 2025 the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office told state officials in writing that the logical discrepancy software was faulty because the 2002 roll had not been digitised accurately.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Commission and the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer did not reply to its questions on the WhatsApp instructions.

issues: Notices and hearings; Duplicates and errors
source: Siasat (IANS, citing officials of the Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal)
what_happened: Officials of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer told IANS that the logical discrepancy check caught people who had falsely linked themselves to unrelated voters, and gave examples they said were found at hearings.

The New Indian Express reported that the Android version of the booth officers' app was updated 31 times between 13 November 2025 and 20 January 2026, with no user manual for the updates, and that officials relied on the app to learn what the revision allowed.
The same report quoted a Chennai booth officer who said the app often froze on her phone, so that data was lost or finished work had to be done again.

The Reporters' Collective reported that hearing notices in West Bengal were generated in bulk by the Commission's software for logical discrepancies, and that two EROs it spoke to, with a few deputies, were signing 4,000 to 5,000 printed notices each day. It reported that the software transliterated names from Bengali into English before matching, so that spellings such as Xalxo and Khalkho triggered a discrepancy. The Collective said this showed the Commission had misled the Supreme Court, where it said there was no automated generation of notices.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Commission had not responded by publication. It set its finding against the Commission's submission to the Court that "There is no automated generation of notices" and that officers were "signing them off after application of mind".

what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that in West Bengal the logical discrepancy check flagged five kinds of mismatch, from spelling differences between the Bengali 2002 roll and the English draft to age gaps with parents and grandparents.
commission_reply: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; District Election Officer
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that a registration officer showed its reporter that the button to clear voters with a name mismatch had disappeared from ERONET since that morning, so such cases now needed the district officer's approval.
commission_reply: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

what_happened: The Indian Express reported that the online Form 6 on the Commission's ECINET portal carried a new declaration asking whether the applicant or their parents or grandparents were in the electoral roll of the last SIR, although the statutory form had not been amended. It reported that although the section was not marked mandatory, applicants could not submit the form without completing it, and that the downloadable Form 6 on the same portal did not include it.
commission_reply: The EC did not respond to a request for comment and Legislative Department Secretary Rajiv Mani could not be reached despite repeated attempts.

what_happened: The Hindu reported that 13 days into the Karnataka SIR only 0.41% of enumeration forms had been submitted online, and that voters complained of captcha failures, server errors and an ECINet search that failed to find records appearing in the published rolls. It reported that online submission required a current mobile number linked to the voter's EPIC.
commission_reply: Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar said the process was still under way. However, the CEO did not comment on the technical glitches reported by voters.

what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported that people filling in enumeration forms on ECINET in Telangana kept being sent back to the home page, and an official put it down to the load from voters in more than a dozen states at once.

issues: Form 6; Commission's independence; Documents and declaration
what_happened: The Indian Express reported, from internal records it investigated, that on May 16 Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi recorded that Form 6 is prescribed by statute and cannot be altered without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and that Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu concurred on May 19. It reported that the declaration was added to the online form anyway, and that on August 13 Sandhu wrote that the changes were unauthorised and illegal and must be removed immediately.

The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi warned on file, from November 2025 to August 2026, that control of the electoral roll software was being centralised in the Commission's IT division. It reported that on August 14 Sandhu wrote that many Chief Electoral Officers, District Election Officers and Electoral Registration Officers had told him they lacked proper and complete access to ERONet, and that on July 29 both Commissioners wrote separately to the Cabinet Secretary about a change in work allocation.
commission_reply: The Election Commission and the two ECs, Sandhu and Joshi, did not respond to calls and questionnaires emailed by The Indian Express seeking comment.

what_happened: The Hindu reported that up to 11 categories of logical discrepancy were being applied in the third phase of the SIR, up from four when the concept was introduced in West Bengal. They include a sibling age gap of nine months or less, which flagged a Delhi resident's twin children, and a marital mapping mismatch where a woman is linked to her father in the old roll and her husband in the new. It reported that the term has never been clearly defined in any official communication.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Goa; Election Commission
issues: Software (ECINET/ERONET); Notices and hearings; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: The Indian Express reported that Goa's Electoral Registration Officers heard electors flagged for logical discrepancies and found 97 of them eligible, but could not reverse the earlier decisions on ECINET because the permission was controlled from Delhi. It reported that the Goa Chief Electoral Officer's office wrote eight times in seven days asking for a rollback option, and that all 97 were missing from the final roll published on February 21 and were still missing on September 20.
commission_reply: Goa's Chief Electoral Officer, Sanjay Goel, told the paper the decision not to include them was the Commission's. The Indian Express later reported that the Commission said, after its meeting of 26 September, that 81 of the 97 had filled Form 6 and that the Chief Electoral Officer had been told to help include them.

what_happened: Commission officials said ECINET is decentralised, that each field officer acts through their own login, and that nobody at headquarters can perform those officers' statutory functions. ERONET is now part of ECINET.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi
issues: Software (ECINET/ERONET); Names left off or deleted; Notices and hearings
what_happened: The Hindu reported that more than 350 Delhi electors had been marked ineligible within a month of hearings, about 200 of them in Vikaspuri, and officials said the marking could not be rolled back by the registration officer or the state's Chief Electoral Officer.
commission_reply: The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer wrote to officers on 25 September 2026 setting a 10-point checklist before marking anyone ineligible and telling them not to delete names on flimsy or frivolous grounds.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Maharashtra; Election Commission
what_happened: Outlook, citing NDTV, reported that Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer S Chockalingam asked for four changes to the ECINET software and more discretion for registration officers in logical discrepancy cases.
commission_reply: The Commission said on 26 September that several portal upgrades had already been made on inputs from state Chief Electoral Officers and that further flexibility needed by field officers would be made operational.

what_happened: The Indian Express reported that on the night of 29 to 30 September 2026 the Commission removed the SIR declaration from the online Form 6 on ECINET for states where the final SIR rolls have been published. It reported that the declaration remained for states where the SIR is still ongoing.
commission_reply: The article cites the Commission's September 26 announcement that ‘for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used’.

what_happened: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh alleged that by restricting registration officers' access to the ECINet roll system and overruling them in Goa, West Bengal and other states, the Commission broke the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
commission_reply: PTI recalled that the Commission, under fire over objections from two of its Commissioners, had said differing views are a normal part of deliberation and that all its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.

issues: Form 6; Names left off or deleted; Documents and declaration
what_happened: The Indian Express reported a letter of 29 September from the Commission’s Secretary ordering a special drive to enrol "left out and young/first time eligible electors" in the 20 states and union territories where the revision is complete, using the statutory Form 6, with the added declaration kept for the revision phase only. It reported that at a video conference with all Chief Electoral Officers, the states were told to compare the roll from before the revision with the one after, list those left off or deleted, visit them at home and help those left out fill in Form 6, with help from the parties’ booth agents.
commission_reply: The letter of 29 September itself was not found. The Commission's letter of 1 October, which continues it, is in the timeline above. The Commission’s press note of 26 September, in the timeline above, had already ordered the drive, and Uttarakhand’s Chief Electoral Officer set out its steps in a press note of 3 October.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi
what_happened: The Hindu reported that the options reached Delhi officers on 30 September and only the ten states and union territories where the third phase was still under way, and that a case marked ineligible still could not be reversed.
commission_reply: The Delhi CEO’s office and the EC did not respond to queries on why the options were introduced at this stage.

issues: Form 6; Documents and declaration; Commission's independence
what_happened: Rahul Gandhi of the Congress, the Leader of the Opposition, said the Chief Election Commissioner had changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. The Commission replied on X that the statement was misleading, that its Bihar order of 24 June 2025 had the Commission's unanimous approval and was upheld by the Supreme Court on 27 May 2026, and that its press note of 26 September said the declaration attached to Form 6 had been upheld, Business Today reported.

The Indian Express reported that at a meeting on 11 August 2026 more than a dozen West Bengal appeal tribunal judges recorded that the Commission's portal did not let them serve notices, hold virtual hearings, restore a deleted voter or give appellants a copy of the order.
commission_reply: The paper said it emailed the Commission and the Registrar General of the Calcutta High Court on 1 October and received no response.

what_happened: Hindustan Times reported that a security researcher emailed CERT-In on 8 July 2026, copied to the Commission's complaints address, about flaws in the voter-services website and the ECINET app. The worst, in the researcher's account, let anyone obtain election officials' names and mobile numbers without logging in.
commission_reply: HT said neither CERT-In nor the Commission answered its questions of 5 October. On 6 October CERT-In told the researcher that one flaw, the hardcoded encryption key he rated least serious, had been fixed and that work on the rest was under progress. HT said none of the flaws related directly to registration officers' access to the roll, and that the email alleged no theft or misuse of data.

what_happened: Congress alleged after the Hindustan Times report that ECINET was designed to centralise deletions and additions from the BJP's headquarters. This is a party's allegation. Hindustan Times had said none of the flaws it reported related directly to registration officers' access to the roll.
commission_reply: Scroll did not report a response from the Commission to this allegation.

what_happened: The security researcher who reported the ECINET flaws told The Wire that CERT-In and the Commission did not reply to him until a Hindustan Times reporter contacted them. CERT-In then said one issue had been resolved, which he said was the most minor. He said the flaws affected at least eight parts of the Commission's systems, including the Suvidha portal and ECORE.
commission_reply: No statement from the Commission was reported.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh; Election Commission; Electoral Registration Officer
issues: Software (ECINET/ERONET); Form 7; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported, from more than 4.3 lakh Form 7 disclosures on the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's website, that 87,127 deletion requests were filed by registration officers and assistant registration officers between 15 March and 2 April 2026 and that none of them gave a reason. Registration officers it spoke to said ERONET generated a Form 7 carrying their digital signature whenever they did not approve a voter at a hearing. It also reported that 1,10,476 deletion requests from individuals were accepted after the deadline.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission had not replied by publication. On 13 October 2026 IANS reported the Chief Electoral Officer's office calling the claims misleading and saying "Notices, hearings, scrutiny and recorded orders preceded action. Pending cases were decided after 6 March as per procedure."

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal; Electoral Registration Officer
issues: Software (ECINET/ERONET); Form 7; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: The Wire reported that 5,38,320 names were deleted from West Bengal's roll between the draft of December 2025 and the final roll of 28 February 2026 through Form 7s that the Commission's software generated in the officer's name when an officer did not approve an elector at a hearing, and that 7,733 more were deleted on Form 7s that people had filed. In the Form 10 registers it read for 284 of the 294 constituencies, 5,23,998 of 5,24,420 Form 7 deletions give the Electoral Registration Officer as the objector and leave the reason blank, and 422 give an individual objector. The Chief Electoral Officer's statement of 6 March 2026 said the state's Form 7 figure included these auto-generated forms, and that the Commission had sent the figure of 5,38,320 by email on 28 February.
commission_reply: The Wire reported that the Additional Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal told it Form 10 gives no option to record details, and that those deleted can apply again through Form 6.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Electoral Registration Officer; Charchagram
what_happened: The Hindustan Times reported a review of ECINET's publicly served code by Saurav Rajput, a data scientist at the civic-tech initiative Charchagram, which found an exception written into the code that can bar Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers in West Bengal from the View Enumeration Form Details tile on the SIR Phase II landing page and from the notice-and-hearing dashboard. The review found no such exclusion for these officers in any other state. The enumeration form page lists each form with its documents and the booth level officer's recommendation, and holds documents labelled as hearing orders. The review read only the code a browser receives before login, on 2, 6, 7 and 9 October and in code fetched on 19 October, so it cannot say whether the rule was ever used, whether the server enforces it, or when it was added. The paper could not verify the review independently.
commission_reply: The Hindustan Times reported that the Election Commission did not answer a questionnaire it sent.

what_happened: The Hindu reported another finding from Saurav Rajput's review of ECINET's code for the civic-tech initiative Charchagram. Behind the official login the portal has an area for managing State Nodal Officers, and each officer's row has a disable button whose confirmation says the user will no longer be able to access the application. Separately, the code carries the message that viewing enumeration form details is not enabled for the selected State, which the review reads as a feature switched on or off State by State. The review read only code the site serves before login. The paper says it was not clear since when the feature has been on the portal, which was launched in January 2026, and the reviewer said he had seen it since 28 September.
commission_reply: The Hindu carried a statement by the Congress general secretary (communications), Jairam Ramesh, that the ECINET system and the Commission's IT division had overruled the statutory authority of Electoral Registration Officers. It reported no response from the Commission.

what_happened: Millennium Post reported that the Trinamool Congress, reacting to the Hindustan Times report of the same day on the West Bengal rule in ECINET's code, asked the Election Commission who had authorised the Bengal-specific changes, why West Bengal was treated differently from other states, who is accountable and what safeguards protect every eligible voter's rights. The party also asked when the Chief Election Commissioner would take responsibility and resign.
commission_reply: The report carries no response from the Commission.

what_happened: The Wire reported three findings from Saurav Rajput's review of ECINET's code for the civic-tech initiative Charchagram, made on 2, 6, 7 and 9 October from code the site serves publicly, with no passwords and no use of ECINET's programming interfaces. Besides the State Nodal Officer controls and the West Bengal rule in the two reports before it, the review found code showing that the officials' portal marks some voters with a gold VIP symbol on the screen that shows the documents in an enumeration form, and a button that downloads a list of these VIP electors by Assembly constituency, which can be narrowed by state, district, constituency and polling part. The criteria for marking a voter are not known. The review cannot say whether any of these features were used, by whom or how often. The Reporters' Collective earlier reported a Mark VIP module in the booth level officers' app, and Charchagram says its review examined the other end of that chain.
commission_reply: The report carries no response from the Commission.

what_happened: In a reply dated 16 October to an RTI application from a social activist in Karimnagar, the Commission declined to give the name and version of the software it used to find errors and anomalies in the rolls during the revision, citing commercial confidence, trade secrets and intellectual property under Section 8(1)(d), the Hindustan Times reported. It called the questions on automatic flagging, artificial intelligence and safeguards against wrongful flagging a clarification outside the definition of information, and cited Section 8(1)(g) on who reviews flagged records.
commission_reply: The Commission said Electoral Registration Officers decide on including or excluding an elector on the basis of facts and records, and that under Sections 13B(1) and 13B(2) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 the officer of each constituency prepares and revises its roll.

places: Pune; Mumbai; Shivajinagar; Malabar Hill; Byculla; Dharavi; Dahisar; Vandre West
parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Maharashtra; District Election Officer; Electoral Registration Officer; Election Commission
issues: Transparency of lists; Notices and hearings; Software (ECINET/ERONET)
what_happened: Lists of electors whose notices were still pending had been published for 39 of Maharashtra's 288 Assembly constituencies, in 14 districts, on the election authorities' websites by Saturday 24 October, The Times of India reported. Officials said the lists hold only unresolved cases and do not cover all 1.22 crore notices generated in the revision. In Pune district only the Shivajinagar list was up, with one elector on it, and in Mumbai the lists for Malabar Hill, Byculla, Dharavi, Dahisar and Vandre West. A circular of 23 October from the Chief Electoral Officer's office told electoral registration officers to download the data from the Commission's ECINET platform, compile one PDF for each constituency, publish it on the district election officer's website by 26 October and share part-wise lists with parties' booth level agents. Officials said documents some electors had given booth level officers during enumeration were not uploaded because the system did not support it then. Notices are to be disposed of by 10 November and the final roll is due on 16 November.
commission_reply: An electoral official said a name on the list does not mean the elector has been finally deleted from the roll, and the report says the Chief Electoral Officer's office will review whether district election authorities have complied with the circular.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal; Appellate tribunal (West Bengal)
what_happened: The appellate tribunals of retired High Court judges that hear appeals in West Bengal's revision have asked the Election Commission at least twice in four weeks to remove an Aadhaar authentication step from its portal, because without it they cannot upload final orders, The Indian Express reported from official records. The screen was added on 21 September, the judges asked in writing on 24 September for it to be removed, and on 13 October the tribunals told the Chief Electoral Officer's office again that the system did not let them upload final orders. Orders are being disposed of on paper and not uploaded. The portal also limits the documents the judges can accept to the 13 the Commission listed for the revision. On 1 October ten of the judges wrote about their working conditions at Joka, about 30 km from Kolkata and New Town, and asked for the tribunals to be moved to a more central place and for an honorarium befitting the judges. They noted that a request to raise it from Rs 25,000 a week to Rs 50,000 had been pending with the Chief Justice since June. The report says the Commission told the Supreme Court that 38.31 lakh appeals had been filed as of 18 September, 22.21 lakh by deleted electors and 16.10 lakh against inclusions, and that 1.26 lakh had been disposed of by 10 September.
commission_reply: The Election Commission did not respond to the paper's queries mailed to its spokesperson on 21 October.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal; Electoral Registration Officer; Congress
issues: Software (ECINET/ERONET); Notices and hearings; Adjudication and appeals
what_happened: Electoral registration officers in Murshidabad had decided almost every hearing case before them by the deadline of 21 February, and a week later far more electors were marked under adjudication and sent to judicial officers than the officers had left pending, The Wire reported from the Commission's ERONET status reports. At 10 pm on 21 February, of 18,84,772 electors called for hearings in the district's 22 constituencies, the officers had parked 18,30,045 for the final roll, found 41,214 ineligible and left 13,513 pending. On 28 February 11,01,145 Murshidabad electors were under adjudication, and judicial officers deleted 4,55,137 of them. In Samserganj 2,391 cases were pending on deadline night, 1,08,400 electors went to adjudication and 74,775 were deleted. Nadia's report of 4:04 am on 22 February shows 57,525 pending, and The Wire puts 2,67,940 of the district's electors under adjudication. An assistant electoral registration officer told The Wire that after hearings closed on 14 February the portal stopped taking document uploads and gained a category, Documents to be reviewed, into which micro-observers and roll observers moved electors the officers had parked for the final roll, and that those the officers then approved again went to adjudication. On 20 February Congress MP Isha Khan Choudhury wrote to the Chief Electoral Officer that the Malda District Magistrate had told an all-party meeting that 5.91 lakh cases had been returned for review that day. Subrata Gupta, the Commission's special roll observer, told The Wire that the observers had recommended a review of lakhs of cases the officers had cleared and that the decisions had to be taken by the registration officers.
commission_reply: On 1 March the Chief Electoral Officer's office posted on X that names were marked under adjudication because the registration officers had not decided them after hearing. On 2 March it posted that it had nowhere said all such cases were due to indecision by the officers, and that a certain number had remained pending and were referred for adjudication. Gupta said the Commission had told the observers that about 60 lakh of about 1.5 crore cases heard were pending and were referred to judicial officers, and that he could not say whether these were the cases marked for review. The Wire says it has written to the Commission and to the current and previous Chief Electoral Officers, and no reply is reported.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal; Booth level officers
what_happened: A screen recording of the Commission's officer portal seen by The Wire shows how the logical discrepancy check flagged a woman in Deganga, North 24 Parganas, born in 1977, The Wire reported. She had named her father and the portal had found him in the 2002 roll. Under the heading 'Logical Discrepancies' the portal gave a single reason, that six other electors had also named the same man as their father, and the only option on the screen was to schedule a hearing. A leader of a booth level officers' association in West Bengal told The Wire that the BLO app changed about 16 times during the revision and that the logical discrepancy system 'was done from Delhi'. The Wire reported that booth level officers were told to verify the flagged electors in person and did so, and the leader said their reports were submitted through the software and no action was taken on them. He said the then Chief Electoral Officer, Manoj Kumar Agarwal, had told the association that his office was forwarding its letters to Delhi and that 'Whatever is being done is being done from Delhi'.
commission_reply: The Wire says it asked Agarwal to confirm the remark the association leader attributes to him and that it will update the report when he replies. No reply is reported.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi; Booth level officers; Election Commission
issues: Software (ECINET/ERONET); Names left off or deleted; Form 6
what_happened: Booth level officers in Delhi have been told to record why eligible electors were marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate at enumeration, and why those traced in the re-verification of the 47.56 lakh names left off the draft of 31 August are unwilling to apply on Form 6 as new voters, The Hindu reported. A Remarks column has been added to the BLO mobile app for the purpose. It is to record why the elector was placed in those categories, whether the person was found at the registered address, and whether an elector found there is already enrolled in another constituency. Officers are to keep count of their visits, the electors found eligible, the Form 6 applications filed and the reasons for not filing. The paper says the instructions follow the Commission's order of 2 October for a special drive to include eligible electors left off the draft, and that the Chief Electoral Officer's directions came nearly a week after the drive was announced. On 30 October officials said they were planning to step up the door-to-door re-verification with all 14,947 booth level officers, and that special camps for students, homeless people, transgender persons and sex workers were being considered for 15 and 22 November, PTI reported.
commission_reply: The instructions are the Chief Electoral Officer's. The report does not say what the recorded reasons will be used for.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh; Electoral Registration Officer; Booth level officers
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that the Commission's manual for processing Form 8 corrections in its software lets an Electoral Registration Officer start a correction on his or her own motion and approve it without field verification or a hearing, so that one officer can start a change, pass over the check and approve it without the voter knowing. It examined the code of the ECINET app and reported that the software let voters' details be changed without booth level officers or other officials having to upload supporting documents. It decompiled ECINET and ERONET and reported that a registration officer could skip the booth level officer's verification and approve a correction request. It also reported that the software does not require officers to keep a record of the changes they make, and that computer operators used ECINET through the officer's login. It reported that the Commission's disclosures of correction forms give only the voter's name and Assembly constituency and no EPIC number, which it said makes it nearly impossible for the public to tell whose entry was changed. The Collective downloaded 12,082 correction forms submitted across Uttar Pradesh between April and September 2026 from the Commission's portal, while the Chief Electoral Officer's own figures put the forms accepted in those months at 33.8 lakh. It said the same manual and software are used for the regular updating of the roll in every state after the SIR.
commission_reply: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer and that neither had replied by publication.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal; Appellate tribunal (West Bengal)
what_happened: The Chief Electoral Officer's office in West Bengal asked the judges of the SIR appellate tribunals in the last week of October to set up digital signature certificates through a private agency, The Indian Express reported from official records. The judges have not logged in to the Commission's portal since they asked on 24 September for its Aadhaar authentication screen to be removed. The agency's email of 28 October to the Chief Electoral Officer lists what each judge must give, which is colour scans of the PAN card and a government identity card, a colour photograph, a mobile number and an email address, the authorising person's government identity card and an authorisation letter. The process also needs one-time passwords sent to the judge's phone and email and a video verification in which the judge shows the original PAN card and identity card. The paper puts the cost of each certificate at Rs 2,300 at the government-notified rate. It reports that the Aadhaar screen was added on 21 September, after the Commission's Director General (IT), Seema Khanna, made a presentation to the judges on changes to the portal, and that the judges have been working offline, according to sources. It says 1.26 lakh of the 38.31 lakh appeals had been disposed of, by the Commission's figures given to the Supreme Court in September.
commission_reply: The report carries no reply from the Election Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer's office.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, Maharashtra; Electoral Registration Officer
issues: Form 6; Software (ECINET/ERONET); Documents and declaration; Notices and hearings
what_happened: The Election Commission has taken the SIR declaration out of the online Form 6 on its ECINet portal in the states where the revision is still running, and the declaration is now on the portal as a separate form, The Indian Express reported on 4 November. The declaration sat between Sections J and K of the online form and asked an applicant to say whether their own name, or a parent's or grandparent's, was on the roll of the last intensive revision, and an applicant could not go on without answering it. The paper reports that the Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52) records a decision of its ER Division of 21 October that the online application would be in two parts, Form 6 and the SIR declaration, as the paper forms are, and that this is what the portal now shows. After the Commission's note of 26 September the declaration had been taken off the online form only in the states where the revision had ended. The paper also reports that four changes to ECINet that Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer, S. Chockalingam, sought in a letter of 24 September have been made. Personal hearings for electors sent notices over mapping or logical discrepancies are now held only in exceptional cases, with booth level officers collecting documents at home. Electors may give documents outside the listed categories. Registration officers can decide logical-discrepancy cases themselves without sending them to the District Election Officer. The upload of an extract from the previous SIR roll is no longer mandatory. The paper reports that applicants filing Form 6 in the special summary revision ordered for 17 states and union territories will not have to fill the SIR declaration. The paper reports that a committee to check whether ECINet complies with the applicable Acts and Rules was constituted by a circular of 14 October. It is headed by a Senior Deputy Election Commissioner and includes a second Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, a Deputy Election Commissioner, a director, four Chief Electoral Officers and two independent experts, from IIT Bombay and IISc Bengaluru. On Goa, the paper reports that the Chief Electoral Officer has been directed to see that the 97 electors left off the final roll are included. It reports that the affidavit says 88 of them have filled in Form 6 and had their applications accepted, that six are out of the country and that three hold Portuguese passports. On West Bengal, the paper reports that the affidavit does not give the number of appeals filed against the inclusion of electors, that the appeals have not been withdrawn, and that the affidavit says the electors concerned are on the rolls and voted in the recent Assembly elections.
commission_reply: The Commission's counter affidavit, as the paper quotes it, maintains that Form 6 was never amended: "There is no substance in the contention that Form 6 has been amended by the Commission vide the SIR Orders." It says the declaration was placed inside the online Form 6 so that an applicant would need a single OTP and a single e-signature.

what_happened: Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer wrote to the Commission asking it to change Form 6 so that electors left off the draft in the revision can register again without declaring themselves first-time voters, Deccan Chronicle reported. The letter says officers find it hard to persuade such electors to sign a form that carries a penalty for a false declaration. It asks for the words "new voters" to be taken out of the form's title, for a separate declaration for people who were enrolled before and are no longer on any roll, and for a place to give the earlier EPIC number.
commission_reply: Officials said that any change to the statutory Form 6 would need the Central government to amend the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. No decision by the Commission was reported.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana; Election Commission; Booth level officers
what_happened: Electoral officials in Telangana attributed the rejection of 1,92,574 of the 5,20,331 Form 6 applications for new enrolment made from 1 January to 14 June 2026, before the revision began, to the absence of the declaration form, The Hindu reported. The paper says the declaration, which asked for details of the applicant or a relative from the 2002 roll or one of 12 listed documents, was made mandatory only for the revision, and that the applications were not decided within a week as the Registration of Electors Rules require. By the figures of the Chief Electoral Officer's office, 3,22,785 of them had been accepted by 28 October and 4,972 were still to be processed. A registration officer told the paper that declaration forms are now being sent door to door through booth level officers so that the pending applications can be processed. Officials said rejected applicants will not be on the final roll unless they apply again.
commission_reply: The paper says the Election Commission announced recently that the declaration is not required with Form 6 in states where the revision is not on, and that this came too late for Telangana. The report carries no other reply.

what_happened: The New Indian Express reported that Rajiv Ranjan Singh, the Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, said on 30 October 2026 that a new panchayat scheme will make Aadhaar-based payments and benefits outdated, and that biometric authentication with the voter identity card number, the EPIC number, will be the only valid way to receive payments and benefits. The paper reported that he said this at a national workshop on the People's Plan Campaign 2026-27 in New Delhi. It reported that a Cabinet committee led by the Prime Minister had approved the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana, which replaces the Rashtriya Gram Swarajya Abhiyan and is to run from 2026-27 to 2030-31.
commission_reply: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj's release on the same workshop, issued through the Press Information Bureau on 31 October 2026 (Release ID 2330751), does not mention the EPIC number, Aadhaar or biometric authentication.
