parties_and_bodies: Booth level officers; Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi
issues: Documents and declaration; Notices and hearings
what_happened: Booth level officers in several Delhi constituencies told The Hindu that registration officers were sending them back to electors who had answered a notice for no mapping with only an Aadhaar card, to collect further documents as proof of citizenship, after the officers had filed field verification reports and undertakings that the electors were eligible and had lived at their addresses for years. One officer said his registration officer called him on 2 November, after he had finished verifying all his cases, and asked him to gather proof of citizenship. Another said the instructions on documents had changed repeatedly. Officers said they had been told at a meeting on 1 October that their undertakings could be accepted where electors had none of the prescribed documents. The Hindu says it saw electors who gave only Aadhaar flagged on the system used by registration officers and their assistants, and an officer said an elector who had given a passport was also asked for documents again. Of nearly 97 lakh electors on Delhi's draft, 33.1 lakh were sent notices, 13.9 lakh for no mapping and the rest for logical discrepancies, and data the Chief Electoral Officer's office shared the week before showed more than 94% of the 33.1 lakh marked for the final roll. The time to decide notices runs to 15 December and the final roll is due on 22 December.
commission_reply: Officials denied that any such instruction had been issued and said no identification or record of 'illegal immigrants' on the roll is being kept. A senior official said that Aadhaar alone was not sufficient, that a registration officer could still mark an elector eligible on a satisfactory field report, and that neither mapping nor logical discrepancies affect an elector's eligibility. Officials said a registration officer not satisfied with the documents could mark an elector ineligible through a speaking order recording the reasons. A registration officer said officials were first told during enumeration to identify foreign nationals on the rolls, that the direction was changed soon after, and that no such list is being prepared.

what_happened: The BBC reported that voters in villages near Patna told it the Bihar draft roll carried wrong photographs, duplicate entries and the name of a person who died more than five years earlier. It reported that in Danara village many residents were not sure officials had visited their homes.
commission_reply: In response to the BBC's questions, the Election Commission shared its 24 June order on conducting the SIR and a 27 July press note outlining efforts to ensure no eligible voter was "left behind". "Further, [the commission] does not take any responsibility of any other misinformation or unsubstantiated allegations being floated around by some vested interests," it added. The BBC also noted the commission has said BLOs worked "very responsibly".

what_happened: The Wire reported that a voter from Ara, Bhojpur, who had been declared dead in the Bihar draft roll, appeared alive in the Supreme Court on 12 August 2025, produced by petitioner Yogendra Yadav. The voter told The Wire he had filled the enumeration form and that the BLO came to his house only after he complained.
commission_reply: Senior advocate Rakesh Dwivedi, for the Commission, called the production of the voter "drama". The bench of Justices Surya Kant and Joymalya Bagchi said there may have been an "inadvertent error", which could be rectified.

what_happened: Scroll reported that its analysis found 200 booths across 58 constituencies in 26 Bihar districts where between 324 and 641 names were left off the draft roll, 77,454 in all. It reported that most of the voters left off whom its team met in 10 of those booths had been marked absent or shifted though they had lived at their addresses for years, and that interviews with 17 BLOs showed no consistent procedure for deciding who was left off.

The graphic Mohammed Zubair posted on X on 1 November (soft-49) shows the same first name, age and five EPIC numbers in Mahadevapura. The Hindu found at least seven EPIC numbers that each appear against two entries in different constituencies, 14 entries in all, three between Mahadevapura and Dasarahalli, three between Mahadevapura and Sarvagnanagar and one between Mahadevapura and Hebbal. In another case an elector left off the draft as permanently shifted applied on Form 6 on 14 August and again on 18 September, according to the Form 9 report, and now appears twice in the final roll, both times at the address from which she had been marked as shifted. The paper notes that Mahadevapura is the constituency over which Rahul Gandhi alleged that more than one lakh votes were fake or stolen in the 2024 Lok Sabha election in Bengaluru Central.
commission_reply: The office of the Chief Electoral Officer said it had received no formal complaints about duplicate entries, that it was watching complaints raised on social media and by political parties, and that the cases would be verified. On 7 November the office explained the cases in a press note and referred them to the district and registration officers for verification (soft-58).

what_happened: The office of Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer said in a statement on 4 November that the roll of every Assembly constituency in the state is to be matched with the electoral rolls of the panchayats and urban local bodies to find eligible people missing from the roll in the special summary revision, The Hindu reported. Electoral Registration Officers are to have Form 6 filled for each eligible person found who is on no Assembly constituency's roll anywhere in India. District Election Officers are also to use the fair price shops run by the Food and Civil Supplies Department, and people aged 18 or more who are registered at a fair price shop in the district and are not on the roll are to be added if found eligible. commission_reply: The directions are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report does not say how the rolls are to be matched or how many electors the matching has found.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
issues: Women; Form 6; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, directed District Election Officers on 4 November to hold a special drive to find and enrol eligible women before the 2027 Assembly election, because the state's rolls hold 1.21 crore fewer women than men, The Times of India reported. By the Commission's data for 7 October 2026 as the paper gives it, the rolls held 13.47 crore electors, of whom 7.34 crore were men, 6.13 crore women and 4,082 third gender electors. The paper puts the gap among women at about 1.71 crore against a projected adult female population of 7.84 crore, and the gap among men at about 99 lakh against a projected adult male population of 8.33 crore. It puts the projected adult population at 16.17 crore, a gap of nearly 2.70 crore from the roll, and says the difference does not necessarily represent eligible people who are not registered. Against a projected 84.47 lakh people aged 18 or 19, 19.62 lakh were registered on 7 October. ASHA workers, auxiliary nurse midwives, anganwadi workers and women of self-help groups are to find eligible women who are not on the roll and help them apply on Form 6 in the special summary revision.
commission_reply: The direction is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report does not say where the projected adult population comes from or how many women the drive is expected to enrol.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh; District Election Officer
what_happened: The number of polling stations in Uttar Pradesh fell by 3,786, from 1,77,516 to 1,73,730, after the Election Commission approved the District Election Officers' proposals for all 403 Assembly constituencies in an exercise carried out on 4 November at the norm of 1,200 electors to a polling station, Hindustan Times reported. He directed District Election Officers to place booth level officers at the approved polling stations and to tell every elector whose polling station has changed in writing through the booth level officer. He also directed that all members of a family be entered in the same section of the roll, and that an elector found at a different polling station from the rest of the family after the draft be corrected on Form 8. The list of approved polling stations is to be given to the representatives of recognised political parties.
commission_reply: The figures are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report does not say how many electors were moved to a different polling station.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh; State Election Commission
what_happened: The Times of India reported on 5 November that the rural panchayat rolls in Uttar Pradesh, finalised on 10 June 2026, hold 12.58 crore electors and the urban local body rolls, published on 2 April 2023, hold 4.33 crore, 16.91 crore in all, against 13.46 crore electors on the Assembly rolls on 7 October 2026, a difference of nearly 3.45 crore. The Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, told the paper that the Assembly rolls hold about 10.20 crore rural electors, about 2.38 crore fewer than the 12.58 crore on the panchayat rolls. The paper puts the urban electors on the Assembly rolls at about 3.36 crore, nearly 97 lakh fewer than the urban local body rolls hold. Rinwa said the panchayat rolls were revised with 1 January 2026 as the qualifying date, while the Assembly rolls also take in people who turn 18 on 1 April, 1 July and 1 October. He said the special summary revision could add more than one crore electors to the roll. He cited a district-level verification carried out after court proceedings involving the two election authorities, which found 144 eligible people missing from the Assembly roll once dead, duplicate, shifted and untraceable electors were excluded, about 7% of the entries examined. The paper says those findings led to the order to compare the Assembly rolls with the panchayat and urban local body rolls across the state (up-32). By the paper's figures the Assembly rolls held 15.4 crore electors before the Special Intensive Revision and 13.39 crore when it ended on 10 April 2026.
commission_reply: Rinwa told the paper that the comparison is not exact, because the municipal rolls were last revised in 2023 and the Assembly rolls are current, and that the differences cannot be taken as eligible people who are not registered, because the rolls may hold dead electors, people who have moved, duplicate entries and other ineligible names. The rural and urban figures as reported, 10.20 and 3.36 crore, make 13.56 crore, 10 lakh more than the 13.46 crore total, and the paper does not explain the difference. The Free Press Journal reports that the State Election Commission prepares the panchayat rolls and the Election Commission of India the Assembly and Lok Sabha rolls, and puts the difference between the panchayat rolls and the rural electors on the Assembly rolls at nearly 2.4 crore.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Haryana; Election Commission
issues: Names left off or deleted; Form 6
what_happened: Nearly 4.5 lakh names were left off Gurgaon's draft roll, which fell from 15.6 lakh electors before the revision to 11 lakh in the draft of 31 July, a fall of 29%, while the city received 40,563 Form 6 applications between 1 June and 30 September, The Times of India reported. The paper says the figures suggest fewer than one application for every 11 names left off, and says the two are not directly comparable, because Form 6 applications include first-time voters. Haryana's Chief Electoral Officer, A. Sreenivas, asked District Election Officers to publicise widely the Commission's clarification of 3 November that an elector missing from the draft roll can apply on Form 6 whatever the earlier enrolment. The paper also reports that hearings had found 12,754 electors ineligible by 28 October and that their names are likely to be deleted from the final roll, due on 30 November, and it does not say whether that figure is the city's or the state's.
commission_reply: The figures for the city are the paper's and are not attributed to an official. The report does not give the 4.5 lakh by reason.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
what_happened: The office of Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer said in a press note of 7 November that The Hindu's report of 803 voter ID numbers linked to 397 people in Mahadevapura after the revision (soft-55) reflected two situations that arose in processing applications. Some applicants filed more than one Form 6 through the Citizen Service Portal during the revision, and because each application was processed separately, more than one EPIC number was generated for the same person. In other cases a Form 8 to shift residence was approved and the elector was added to the roll of the new constituency, while the Form 7 to delete the entry in the old constituency stayed pending, because roll operations were frozen by law for the final publication. The office said the cases had been referred to the District Election Officers, Additional District Election Officers and Electoral Registration Officers for verification and remedial action under the law. Mohammed Zubair's post of 1 November described an elector in Mahadevapura who submitted Form 6 twice and now has five EPIC numbers (soft-49). The press note does not mention the post.
commission_reply: The note is the Chief Electoral Officer's own reply. Vartha Bharati reports that it gives no count of the electors affected or of the entries marked for deletion, no date for the corrections, and does not say whether the final rolls are affected. Karnataka's final roll was published on 27 October.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; State Election Commission; Booth level officers
issues: Living electors marked dead; Names left off or deleted; Duplicates and errors
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported on 7 November that 1,82,440 electors whom the Election Commission marked dead and left off the draft roll in Rajasthan's Special Intensive Revision are on the State Election Commission's panchayat roll as living electors. The Collective compared the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors, on which about 8.75 lakh people were marked dead, with the panchayat roll by each elector's voter ID and EPIC number, and checked a sample against the State Election Commission's own search portal. The two rolls were revised in parallel. The Commission finished its revision on 21 February 2026 and the State Election Commission finished its own four days later, and the panchayat draft roll was published after the Commission had published its list. By the Collective's chart of ten constituencies, the most such electors were in Garhi (4,889), Sirohi (4,624), Banswara (4,549) and Ghatol (4,429). The Collective says it did not verify on the ground which of the two commissions is right. It downloaded both rolls in October, when polling for the panchayats had begun in four phases. It says it could not check the Commission's monthly updates to the roll since the revision, because the Commission does not say whether an elector once marked dead and later restored keeps the same voter ID. Two booth level officers it spoke to denied the discrepancy, and the Collective says its analysis shows they were wrong.
commission_reply: The Collective says it sent detailed questions to the Commission and to Rajasthan's State Election Commission and had no answer. The report does not say how many of the 1,82,440 are eligible electors, or whether any of them have been added back to the Commission's roll since the final roll. Amar Ujala reported on 8 November that the State Election Commission used the Commission's roll from before the revision as the base roll for the local body and panchayat elections (soft-57).

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
parties_and_bodies: State Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, Rajasthan
issues: Names left off or deleted; Transparency of lists
what_happened: Amar Ujala reported on 8 November that the roll Rajasthan's State Election Commission used for the local body elections holds about 5.45 crore electors, against about 5.15 crore on the Election Commission's final roll after the Special Intensive Revision, a difference of about 30 lakh. The social activist Nikhil Dey told the paper that the Commission's roll held about 5.47 crore electors in Rajasthan before the revision and about 5.15 crore after it, about 32 lakh fewer. He said the State Election Commission has the right to prepare its own roll for its elections and had always taken the latest roll from the election department, but took the roll from before the revision for the urban local body and panchayat elections, a roll on which the revision found about 1.80 lakh electors dead. He said the State Election Commission told his group that its election process had begun well before, and did not agree to an audit his group asked for, and that the group is seeking the information under the RTI Act. He asked how one booth level officer could mark an elector dead on one roll while the name stayed on the other, and asked for the difference to be looked into. The Reporters' Collective reported a day earlier that 1,82,440 electors the Commission marked dead are on the State Election Commission's panchayat roll as living electors, on a roll it describes as revised in parallel with the Commission's (soft-59).
commission_reply: The State Election Commission's report, as the paper gives it, says the preparations for the local body elections began well before, and the Commission's roll from before the revision was used as the base roll for that reason. The Chief Electoral Officer, Naveen Mahajan, said the State Election Commission relied on the roll from before the revision, and that no objection had been raised about the final roll of the revision in Rajasthan. The report does not say how many of the 30 lakh are on the local body roll and not on the final roll, or how many of them are eligible.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
parties_and_bodies: BJP; Samajwadi Party; Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh
issues: Names left off or deleted; Minorities
what_happened: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Minister, Yogi Adityanath, said at the Aaj Tak Panchayat programme in Ayodhya on 8 November that about 1.27 crore Hindu voters whose names are on the electoral rolls of the state's panchayat elections are missing from the Election Commission's rolls after the revision, and that the number of Muslim voters in the state rose by 1.65% after it, The Indian Express reported. In his words as the paper gives them, 66 lakh such voters are on the panchayat rolls, 55 lakh are Hindu voters who receive the benefits of government welfare schemes and are missing from the rolls, and 4.5 lakh are aged 18 or 19 and are missing from the rolls. He said a memorandum had been given to the Commission asking why this happened, and he appealed for these names to be included. Asked in the interview where the figure came from, he said that the rolls from before and after the revision are with everyone, in Aaj Tak's video of the interview. ThePrint reports him saying that about 46 lakh dead electors were on the rolls before the revision, and India Today and Aaj Tak report him saying that the names of about 46 lakh dead electors should be removed and the names of eligible voters should also be included.
commission_reply: The Samajwadi Party president, Akhilesh Yadav, asked reporters how the Chief Minister had figures of electors by religion when the Commission had released none, ThePrint reported. In a post on X on 9 November he asked that Aadhaar be linked with voting, that metal cards be issued in place of paper or plastic voter cards, and that fingerprints or iris scans be used to identify voters, and he said the BJP would then be unable to have bogus votes cast. The party's spokesperson, Udaiveer Singh, asked the Chief Minister to explain how he got the data and to demand action against the Chief Election Commissioner and the state's Chief Electoral Officer, The Indian Express reported. The Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, said he would answer all questions on the revision on 17 November, after the draft roll of the special summary revision is published. No reply from the Commission was reported.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
parties_and_bodies: District Election Officer; Booth level officers
what_happened: The Ghaziabad district administration will use the Census 2027 enumeration to find residents aged 18 or more who are not on the electoral roll and put them in touch with booth level officers to enrol, The Times of India reported. The decision was taken on 9 November at a meeting chaired by the District Magistrate and District Election Officer, Ravindra Kumar Mandar, to review preparations for the Census and the special summary revision. The paper reports that 5.7 lakh names (20.2%) went off Ghaziabad's roll in the revision, and 3.16 lakh in the Sahibabad constituency, which it says is the highest of any constituency in the state. It gives the Census self-enumeration as running from 16 to 30 November and the house-to-house enumeration from 1 December to 4 January. The meeting also reviewed the polling stations, and by the list the Commission approved the district, with the part of the Dhaulana constituency that falls in it, will have 865 polling centres and 3,073 polling stations.
commission_reply: The decision is the District Election Officer's own. The report does not say how the names found in the Census are to reach the booth level officers.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
parties_and_bodies: Biju Janata Dal; District Election Officer; Government of Odisha; Government of Andhra Pradesh
what_happened: The Biju Janata Dal alleged at a press conference on 11 November that residents of villages on the border of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh still held voter identity cards issued by both states after Odisha's revision, and asked how residents of Kotia in Koraput district and Jumdang village in Malkangiri district could remain registered in two states, Hindustan Times reported. The party's senior leader Devi Prasad Mishra said the law does not allow a person to be registered in two places, and asked that Odisha's Chief Electoral Officer seek from the Andhra Pradesh government the number of Odisha residents who had voted in that state's elections. He also asked why Andhra Pradesh had not removed from its rolls duplicate electors and electors the party alleges are ineligible. The Koraput Collector, Manoj Satyawan Mahajan, said some residents of Kotia had crossed into Andhra Pradesh to vote in its panchayat elections the week before, and that about 10% of Kotia's voters had voted there. He said the 40% turnout that Andhra Pradesh officials gave was the combined turnout at a polling booth serving several villages, some of them in Andhra Pradesh, and that the district administration had prevented Andhra Pradesh from setting up a polling booth inside Kotia. Odisha's Law Minister, Prithiviraj Harichandan, said the state government would look into the matter and that the Revenue Department needs to identify people holding voter identity cards from both states and take legal action against them.
commission_reply: The report gives no reply from Odisha's Chief Electoral Officer, from Andhra Pradesh's or from the Commission, and no count of electors registered in both states. The Collector's 10% is the share of Kotia's voters he says voted in Andhra Pradesh, and the report does not say how many of them are on Odisha's roll.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
issues: Names left off or deleted; Duplicates and errors; Form 6
what_happened: Uttar Pradesh's panchayat rolls hold 12.58 crore electors against 10.20 crore rural electors on the Assembly rolls, 2.38 crore fewer, and the urban local body rolls hold 4.32 crore against 3.31 crore urban electors on the Assembly rolls, more than one crore fewer, Live Hindustan reported on 11 November. Together the panchayat and local body rolls hold 16.90 crore electors and the Assembly rolls 13.52 crore, and the paper reports the difference as 3.38 crore electors missing from the Assembly rolls. It reports that the Election Commission has ordered the three sets of rolls to be matched, and that the matching follows an inquiry ordered by the High Court in Makdoompur village in Rae Bareli. Makdoompur's panchayat roll held 1,987 electors, of whom 1,549 were on the Assembly roll. After the matter was taken to the High Court, 448 electors missing from the Assembly roll were examined on the Court's direction. By the paper's account the Commission found that 44 of them had been moved to a neighbouring polling station and 290 were ineligible, shifted or duplicate, and 114 were eligible electors living in the village who were on the panchayat roll and off the Assembly roll, and their names were added. The paper says Form 6 is now being filled to enrol such electors. By its figures the Assembly rolls hold 7.37 crore men and 6.15 crore women, 834 women to every 1,000 men, and 2.04 crore names of dead, shifted and absent electors were cut in the revision.
commission_reply: The report does not name the case in the High Court or date its order, and it does not date the Commission's order to match the rolls or say how the matching is to be done. It gives no date for its count of the Assembly rolls. No reply from the Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer is reported. The Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, has said he will answer questions on the revision on 17 November (up-34).

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Government of Uttar Pradesh; Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh; Electoral registration officers; District Election Officer
what_happened: Uttar Pradesh's Appointment Department has named the Moradabad Divisional Commissioner, Sangeeta Singh, on the Election Commission's direction, as the officer to hold an administrative inquiry against Mayank Goswami and Hemant Kumar Chaudhary, who were Sub-Divisional Magistrates of Pilibhit at the time and were suspended on allegations of malpractice in the revision of the roll of the Pilibhit Sadar constituency, Amar Ujala reported on 12 November. She is to go to Pilibhit soon, take the records and an account of events from the officials concerned, and then examine the allegations. The department's letter on the inquiry has been sent to the Pilibhit and Moradabad administrations. The paper recalls that after complaints about the constituency's roll in October the District Election Officer, Alok Kumar, sent the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, an inquiry report that found irregularities in the disposal of 13,779 offline forms received between 31 May and 28 August, of which 10,470 were accepted and 3,309 rejected. On that report and the Chief Electoral Officer's letter, the Commission decided on 31 October to suspend the two officers, said they could not be reinstated without its prior permission, and wrote to the Chief Secretary for action.
commission_reply: The inquiry is the state government's, on the Commission's direction. The report does not date the Appointment Department's letter or set a time for the inquiry, and it carries no reply from the two officers.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
places: Murshidabad; Farakka; Purba Bardhaman; South 24 Parganas
parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal; Election Commission
what_happened: The office of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer told the Registrar General of the Calcutta High Court in memos dated 12 October and 29 October 2026 that judicial officers had not decided 815 adjudication cases and had decided 5,004 more without e-signing them, The Wire reported on 13 November. The two figures add to 5,819, which is the 'around 6,000' of The Wire's headline. The Wire publishes the memo of 12 October, No. 9806-Home (Elec) from the Additional Chief Electoral Officer. It says the Commission's IT team wrote on 6 August that the logins of the judicial officers of the constituencies concerned had been reactivated, and it asks the Registrar General to have those officers e-sign the decided cases and decide the rest at the earliest. It refers to an earlier memo of 7 August. The Wire reports that the memo of 29 October gives the same two figures, and that the office asked district election officers the same day to report on these cases by 3 November, before the integrated draft roll of the special summary revision due on 23 November. The Wire says the Commission's ECINET report 'Individuals Under Adjudication' of 9 April, which it has seen, records 22,163 cases that judges had not decided when the judicial review ended and 83,504 that they had decided and not signed, 44,027 of them found eligible. It reports that 12,337 of the undecided cases were in Murshidabad, 5,194 in Purba Bardhaman and 3,374 in South 24 Parganas, across 67 constituencies, with 3,183 in Farakka. The Wire's own count, from the rolls of 304 polling stations in 11 of Murshidabad's 22 constituencies, is 29,347 electors still marked under adjudication, which it says is five times the number the Chief Electoral Officer's office gives for the whole state. In three polling stations of Mahadebnagar gram panchayat in Farakka, whose roll as revised up to 6 April it has seen, it counts 1,914, and booth level officers told it that the judicial review there never took place. The Wire says an elector whose case was never decided has no order to take to the appellate tribunals and was not able to vote in April.
commission_reply: The Wire says it asked the Chief Electoral Officer on 5 November why 22,163 cases had not been decided by the time the roll was frozen, when and by whom they were decided while the judicial officers' logins were inactive, and how many of those electors were found eligible, and that it will update the report on a reply. It gives no response from the Chief Electoral Officer's office, the Election Commission or the High Court.

parties_and_bodies: Booth level officers; Police; Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu
what_happened: The Indian Express reported the deaths of two BLOs. The family of a BLO in Kannur, Kerala, alleged he was under pressure to finish by December 4, and police said a note found on a BLO in Jaipur said he faced extreme pressure from his supervisor and was told he would be suspended if he did not meet his SIR target. It also reported that revenue employees in Tamil Nadu announced a statewide boycott of SIR work over workload.
commission_reply: Kannur District Collector Arun K Vijayan's report indicated that the BLO was not under any work pressure. The Indian Express said its multiple calls and messages to Rajasthan CEO Naveen got no response.

parties_and_bodies: Booth level officers; District Election Officer
what_happened: The Indian Express reported that two women assistant BLOs died of heart attacks in Tapi and Vadodara districts, bringing BLO deaths in Gujarat that week to four. The husband of one said she was a heart patient who had asked to be excused from BLO duty, which the Vadodara Collector disputed.
commission_reply: Vadodara District Collector Anil Dhameliya said, “We checked with the institute as well as with the local officials. She had not made any official request to be excused (from BLO duty)… We have learnt now that she was suffering from a heart ailment and had episodes of fainting in her institute as well.” He also said, “We have been cautious about ensuring that there is no excessive workload on the BLOs and therefore, we have appointed additional staff to assist in the process.” An unnamed government official said, “With a large workforce of over two lakh involved in the SIR work, these deaths can be termed as natural. Linking these to SIR is not justified and logical.”

parties_and_bodies: Police; Electoral Registration Officer; Booth level officers
issues: Deaths; BLO workload; Police and FIRs
what_happened: The New Indian Express reported four deaths of officers on revision duty in Uttar Pradesh that families tied to workload. They were a lekhpal supervisor in Fatehpur who died by suicide a day before his wedding, after what his family said were threats of dismissal, a teacher who collapsed on duty in Bareilly, a teacher in Gonda who died by suicide and an officer in Lucknow who had a brain haemorrhage. In Fatehpur police registered an FIR for abetment against a revenue officer and unnamed officials.
commission_reply: The paper reported, citing unnamed sources, that the family had first named the electoral registration officer and was made to change the complaint, which the Additional Superintendent of Police, Fatehpur, denied.

parties_and_bodies: District Election Officer; Booth level officers; Election Commission
issues: Deaths; BLO workload; Schedule and deadlines
what_happened: A 46-year-old assistant teacher on booth officer duty since 7 October died by suicide at home in Moradabad, police said, leaving a note to the district Basic Education Officer saying he could not meet the SIR targets, India Today reported.
commission_reply: The District Magistrate said "Preliminary information suggests he died by suicide. His quality of work was excellent. Anganwadi employees were deployed to assist him. Both administrative and police probes are underway." The Commission extended the SIR schedule by a week the same day.

parties_and_bodies: District Election Officer; Booth level officers
what_happened: A 40-year-old assistant teacher working as a booth officer in Hathras collapsed at home and died on the way to hospital, The Telegraph reported. His family said he had been under stress since starting the work. The paper counted three booth officer deaths in Uttar Pradesh since the previous Sunday.
commission_reply: The District Magistrate called the death unfortunate, said the cause would be clear after the post-mortem, and said the administration would explore a job for the officer's wife.

what_happened: The BBC reported that 10 BLOs it spoke to in Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal said they worked 14 to 15 hours a day with little rest, and that families linked the deaths of more than a dozen poll workers, by alleged suicide or heart attack, to election work stress. The BBC said it had not independently verified the causes of death. It reported BLOs saying the SIR app crashed often and that many had not been paid.
commission_reply: The BBC said the Commission did not answer its questions. It cited media reports of a court affidavit in which the Commission called claims linking booth officers' deaths to the revision "false, exaggerated and politically motivated".

what_happened: The Indian Express reported that a 75-year-old man died of cardiac arrest, according to hospital sources, after falling ill in a queue for an SIR hearing at the Rampurhat-1 block office in Birbhum. His wife and family alleged the SIR process had caused him excessive stress and held the Election Commission responsible. It also reported that an elderly man died of cardiac arrest at an SIR hearing in Howrah the previous day.

issues: Deaths; Notices and hearings; Police and FIRs
what_happened: The New Indian Express, citing PTI, reported that police in Purulia registered an FIR on a complaint by the son of an 82-year-old man who died allegedly by suicide on 29 December hours before he was due at an SIR hearing. An officer was quoted as saying the case included charges of abetment of suicide and criminal conspiracy against Election Commission officials, with no official named. The family alleged he acted out of anxiety over the SIR.
